items.summary: US Consumer Confidence fell to 89.4 (7-month low) vs 90.2 in July. Expectations Index dropped 5.8 pts to 68.2 (deep in recession-warning territory); Present Situation +6.8 to 121.2 as jobs-plentiful ticked up to 27.0%.

explainer.tagline: Consumer confidence slips to a 7-month low as forward expectations deteriorate even while current-conditions read improves.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Conference Board's monthly Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 was released at 10am ET Tuesday. Headline dipped 0.8 points to 89.4 (a seven-month low), below the 90.2 consensus and prior reading. The split within the survey tells the story.
explainer.howItWorks: The Present Situation Index rose 6.8 points to 121.2 after three months of decline, driven by improved labor-market perceptions (share saying jobs are 'plentiful' rose to 27.0% from 24.4%). But the Expectations Index — the six-months-ahead gauge — dropped 5.8 points to 68.2, extending its stay well below the 80 threshold historically associated with a coming recession. 12-month inflation expectations ticked up.
explainer.whyItMatters: The divergence — 'right now feels ok, six months from now looks bad' — is exactly the shape that has preceded consumer-spending softening in prior cycles. Consumer-discretionary desks read the print alongside DKS's guidance cut this morning; both point at more caution in H2 discretionary spend.

items.summary: US new single-family home sales fell 10.5% M/M in July to a 607K SAAR (-6.3% Y/Y); median price dropped 2.3% M/M to $393.8K; supply of unsold new homes climbed to 9.6 months at current sales rate.

explainer.tagline: US new-home sales fall 10.5% in July to a 607K annualized pace — biggest monthly drop this year; unsold inventory swells to 9.6 months.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Census Bureau and HUD released July 2026 New Residential Sales data at 10am ET Tuesday. The seasonally-adjusted annualized rate came in at 607K, versus 678K in June, a 10.5% month-over-month decline and 6.3% below the July 2025 rate of 648K.
explainer.howItWorks: The median sales price fell to $393.8K, 2.3% below June's $403.1K and 0.9% below year-ago — builders continuing to cut price to keep contracts alive. Unsold new-home inventory stood at 488K at end-July, equating to 9.6 months of supply at the current pace (well above the ~6-month 'balanced' benchmark). Interestingly the average price was $508.8K, up 4.1% M/M — the median/average divergence points to a mix-shift toward larger homes among what did sell.
explainer.whyItMatters: Builders are getting squeezed at both ends: sales pace decelerating and supply rising. Read alongside yesterday's slower Case-Shiller resales prints, the picture is one where the housing market is quietly cooling. Watch LEN, DHI, TOL, PHM, KBH plus building-products names (BLD, IBP, FBIN) into fall.
explainer.forWho: housing analysts, rates strategists

3. **9.6 months of supply is well above the ~6-month 'balanced' benchmark** — builders will likely stay in promotional-pricing mode through fall.

Next catalysts: PCE inflation prints Aug 26; homebuilder Q3 reports (LEN, KBH) later this cycle.

items.summary: Memory names crack Monday after weekend Wccftech report says Trump admin will let Apple source Chinese DRAM (CXMT) and NAND (YMTC) after the Trump-Xi September summit. SNDK -6.45%, MU -5.83%, WDC -5.24%.

explainer.tagline: Wccftech report that Trump will let Apple buy CXMT DRAM and YMTC NAND after the Xi summit knocks 5–7% off the U.S. memory complex.
explainer.whatIsIt: Weekend reporting from Wccftech says the Trump administration is prepared to sign off on Apple sourcing memory from ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT, DRAM) and Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp (YMTC, NAND), with the announcement expected after Trump and Xi meet in the U.S. around late September. Both Chinese chipmakers are on the Pentagon's Section 1260H 'Chinese military companies' list and YMTC is on the Commerce Department's Entity List. Apple has told the White House Chinese sourcing 'could help us on the supply side and perhaps the pricing side.'
explainer.howItWorks: Monday close: SanDisk -6.45% to $1,493.12, Micron -5.83% to $910.43, Western Digital -5.24% to $435.38. Yahoo Finance and 24/7 Wall St flag the story as the driver; The Motley Fool notes Micron dropped 5.5% in the first five minutes of trading after the Wccftech piece hit weekend timelines. Per the reporting, DRAM/NAND sourced from CXMT and YMTC would initially only be used in Apple products sold inside China. Lynx Equity's KC Rajkumar calls the selloff an 'overreaction,' noting CXMT lacks iPhone qualification and YMTC has committed newest NAND capacity to domestic customers.
explainer.whyItMatters: SanDisk had run 572% YTD into Friday's close and Micron/WDC had ridden the same memory-AI bid, so the tape is now pricing a real Chinese competitor gaining Apple's blessing — even a partial, China-only carve-out reprices future ASPs and margins across NAND and DRAM. It also sits inside the broader U.S.–China diplomatic setup around the September summit: markets read this as a signal Washington may trade export controls for deal wins. Watch iPhone 18 Pro memory BOM commentary and any pushback from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who publicly opposed Apple's plan on Aug 14.
explainer.forWho: Semis traders, Apple supply-chain analysts, China policy desks.

items.summary: HIMS -7.99% to $31.08 after Bloomberg says Visa enrolled the telehealth co in its Acquirer Monitoring Program on July chargeback surge in weight-loss subscriptions. Must cut dispute rate under 1.5% for 3 straight months to exit; ~$75K bill lands in September.

metrics.Notification: Via processor Stripe earlier in August

explainer.tagline: Bloomberg scoops that Visa put HIMS in its Acquirer Monitoring Program after a July weight-loss chargeback spike; stock -8% to $31.08 Monday.
explainer.whatIsIt: Bloomberg reported Thursday Aug 21 that Visa enrolled Hims & Hers in its Acquirer Monitoring Program (VAMP) after credit-card disputes in the company's weight-loss GLP-1 subscription business surged past Visa's 1.5% acceptable threshold in July. Visa notified HIMS through its payment processor Stripe earlier this month. To exit VAMP, HIMS has to hold its dispute rate below 1.5% for three consecutive months.
explainer.howItWorks: HIMS closed -7.99% at $31.08 on Monday Aug 24, down $2.70 from Friday's $33.78 close — the ticker's worst session in about a month. Under VAMP, HIMS pays an $8 surcharge per disputed transaction; Bloomberg estimates the first bill lands in September at roughly $75,000. A Hims spokesperson told Bloomberg the company sees 'a relatively small number of disputed charges' and that checkout clearly discloses membership and medication costs. Barclays trimmed its price target to $35 from $39 on Aug 21 flagging billing/cancellation risk.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the second regulatory hit on Hims' subscription plumbing inside a month: the FTC on July 29 alleged deceptive billing and cancellation practices tied to weight-loss subscriptions. VAMP escalates that into direct payments-network scrutiny — if HIMS can't drive disputes back under 1.5% inside three months, it risks higher penalties, forced product/checkout changes, or processor pressure that touches the core telehealth subscription economics. The stock's implied vol and short interest already reflect a fragile setup around the GLP-1 subscription business.
explainer.forWho: Digital-health longs, GLP-1 supply-chain watchers, subscription-economics traders.

2. **Barclays cut PT to $35 from $39 on Aug 21** citing billing/cancellation risk.
3. **Structural risk to the subscription model** — if disputes stay elevated, HIMS faces bigger penalties, forced UX changes at checkout, or pressure from Stripe/other processors.

Company told Bloomberg it sees 'a relatively small number of disputed charges' and disclosures at checkout are clear.

Next catalysts: September penalty bill, next monthly dispute-rate data, FTC docket.

items.summary: Optical-networking supplier AAOI drops 13.77% to $107.63 on Monday after Friday's 8-K reveals a fresh $600M ATM stock program with Raymond James & Needham — dilution fears take the tape as the largest ATM the company has ever run.

explainer.tagline: Friday 8-K launches a $600M ATM stock program; Monday tape rerates AAOI down almost 14% on dilution risk.
explainer.whatIsIt: AAOI disclosed on Friday Aug 21 an Equity Distribution Agreement with Raymond James & Associates and Needham & Company allowing the company to sell up to $600 million of common stock via at-the-market sales into the open market from time to time. Shares can be sold on Nasdaq Global Market or other venues, with AAOI controlling timing, size, and minimum price via placement notices. The company is not obligated to sell any shares and can suspend sales at any time; agents get a 2% commission on gross sales.
explainer.howItWorks: Monday close: AAOI -13.77% to $107.63, off $17.19 from Friday's $124.82. Filing is under an automatic shelf registration statement Form S-3ASR (Registration No. 333-283905) with a prospectus supplement filed Aug 21. items.summary: Trump escalates the Canada trade war 48 hours after Section 338 duties took effect: autos and light trucks jump from 25% to 50%, auto parts get a new 50% duty, steel stays at 50%, all live Jan 1 2027. PM Carney: 'We got attacked.'

explainer.tagline: Trump doubles Canada auto tariff to 50% and slaps a new 50% duty on auto parts, effective Jan 1, 2027.
explainer.whatIsIt: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social Monday Aug 24 that the US will double tariffs on 'all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel' from Canada to 50%, effective Jan 1, 2027. The escalation lands 48 hours after Section 338 tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods went live at midnight Aug 22, and after weekend negotiations to trim the auto rate to 15% collapsed on Sunday over what Trump called 'walk backs' by Canada.
explainer.howItWorks: Autos and light trucks currently face a 25% Trump-era duty; the announcement doubles that to 50%. Auto parts get a new 50% duty from a base of 0%. Steel stays at the 50% level already imposed Aug 22. Trump on Truth Social: 'On Trade... they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with.' PM Mark Carney told a press conference: 'You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked.' Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened counter-measures including restrictions on electricity and critical-mineral exports to the US.
explainer.whyItMatters: The Big Three (F, GM, STLA) run deeply integrated cross-border assembly through Windsor and Oshawa; a 50% duty on both finished vehicles and parts would break the current landed-cost stack for pickup trucks and small SUVs assembled in Canada. Steel-consuming names (autos, appliances, homebuilders) already pricing 50% Aug-22 duties would see a second stack. Retaliation risk: Ontario controls the Quebec-hydro-adjacent grid feeding upstate NY + Midwest; a critical-mineral cutoff would hit US battery supply chains.

Tesla's chief engineer told the NTA hearing the company would be 'extremely happy' to have ~2,500 vehicles on the road within a year, framing the 5,000 figure as a regulatory ceiling, not a deployment target.

items.org: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
items.summary: Talks broke down minutes before the midnight deadline Friday; 50% Section 338 duties on cement, hockey sticks, softwood lumber and other Canadian goods took effect Saturday. Carney called last-minute US changes 'unfair', suspended talks and promised matching tariffs.

explainer.tagline: First-ever Section 338 tariffs — 50% duties on ~$20B of Canadian goods live after Friday-night talks collapse.
explainer.whatIsIt: US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed shortly before a midnight Friday deadline, sending previously-paused Section 338 tariffs live at 12:01 a.m. ET on Saturday, Aug 22 2026. The duties add a 50% surcharge on roughly $20 billion of Canadian imports — a list that includes cement, softwood lumber, hockey sticks, certain building materials, liquors and specific apparel categories. Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended talks and said Canada would match the tariffs dollar for dollar.
explainer.howItWorks: The 50% duty is imposed under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — a statute that has never been used by a president since it became law and lets the White House hit any trading partner that 'discriminates' against US commerce with duties of up to 50%. Trump had originally proclaimed the tariffs to take effect Aug 19, then paused them 3 days as negotiators worked. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said 'new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada' broke the deal; Carney's office said late US changes were 'unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal.'
explainer.whyItMatters: First presidential use of Section 338 opens a new legal channel for tariff action after the Supreme Court struck down the earlier IEEPA-based duties in February. Canadian retaliation on the same $20B scale escalates the trade war heading into the Labor Day week and Jackson Hole. Watch autos (Big Three US-Canada supply chains), softwood-lumber-linked housing names, and USD/CAD — the loonie is likely to open weaker Monday as the retaliation list drops.

* Coverage: ~$20B of Canadian imports — cement, hockey sticks, softwood lumber, some building materials, liquors, certain apparel
* Legal basis: **Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930** — the first time a president has ever invoked it since the statute passed
* Trump had originally set the tariffs live Aug 19, then paused them 3 days for negotiation
* PM Mark Carney: last-minute US changes 'unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal'

items.summary: August flash composite PMI rose to 56.0 from 54.5, the strongest US business expansion since April 2022. Services 56.8 blew past 54.0 est; manufacturing 53.2 slipped from 53.9 as supply delays lengthened.

explainer.tagline: US private-sector activity hit its fastest pace since April 2022 in August, all on the services side.
explainer.whatIsIt: S&P Global's flash Purchasing Managers' Index for August is a first look at private-sector business activity, based on survey responses collected mid-month. The composite output index came in at 56.0, up from 54.5 in July — the strongest reading in more than four years. Services (56.8) was well above the 54.0 consensus, while manufacturing (53.2) missed the 53.9 estimate and cooled to a 13-month low.
explainer.howItWorks: PMI values above 50 indicate expansion. The composite blends manufacturing output and services activity into a single number. In August, services activity ran at its fastest pace since December 2024 while goods production posted its weakest increase in 13 months, partly on fading safety-stock building and lengthening supply-chain delays (worst in about four years). Employment grew at the fastest pace since early 2025, and business expectations for the next 12 months reached a nine-month high. Input-cost inflation stayed elevated on energy, but selling-price inflation moderated.
explainer.whyItMatters: S&P Global's chief business economist Chris Williamson wrote that 'US business is booming, with firms reporting the fastest output growth for over four years so far in the third quarter,' consistent with GDP tracking near 3% annualized in Q3 versus 1.5% in Q2. A strong growth signal five days before Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech reduces the odds of near-term Fed easing and helps explain the Aug 21 curve reaction — 10Y yields ticked higher on the print, but equities held (Dow +0.98% to 53,277; S&P 500 +0.43% to 7,674) as services momentum and hiring reassured on demand.

explainer.tagline: MRNA nearly triples on Wed Aug 19 as the first Phase 3 mRNA cancer therapy readout — intismeran + KEYTRUDA — cuts melanoma recurrence.
explainer.whatIsIt: Moderna and Merck reported positive Phase 3 topline data from the INTerpath-001 trial pairing intismeran autogene (an individualized mRNA neoantigen therapy previously known as mRNA-4157 / V940) with Merck's KEYTRUDA in patients with completely resected stage IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma. The combination met the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival versus KEYTRUDA alone. It is the first successful Phase 3 readout for any mRNA-based cancer therapy.
explainer.howItWorks: INTerpath-001 randomized 1,137 patients 2:1 to intismeran (1 mg every three weeks, up to nine doses) plus KEYTRUDA (400 mg every six weeks, up to nine cycles for ~1 year) versus KEYTRUDA alone. The trial hit its RFS primary endpoint and DMFS key secondary; overall survival remains a secondary. The Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 readout previously showed a 49% reduction in the risk of recurrence or death versus KEYTRUDA monotherapy. MRNA closed at $174.38 (+176.97%) on volume of 199.3M shares (~19× the three-month average); MRK closed +12.6% at $152.20; BNTX +21.96% at $113.12.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the platform-validating readout the mRNA-oncology thesis has been waiting for since KEYNOTE-942 — a bona fide Phase 3 win that re-anchors the value of Moderna's cancer pipeline, restarts talk of a broader neoantigen platform beyond melanoma, and lifts mRNA peers (BNTX). Merck said it plans to begin regulator talks within months, which could open a large adjuvant-melanoma addressable market as an add-on to already-approved KEYTRUDA. The scale of the MRNA move (near-tripling, $44B added) reflects both the trial result and short-covering after a multi-year drawdown.

items.summary: July 28–29 FOMC minutes released Wed Aug 19 show the Committee held 9-3 at 3.50–3.75% with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting for a 25bp hike; participants judged 'policy tightening would likely be necessary' if inflation doesn't cool.

explainer.tagline: July FOMC minutes reveal the most fractured Fed vote in years: 9-3 hold, three dissenters preferring a 25bp hike, and Chair Warsh floating a six-meeting-a-year calendar.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Fed released the minutes of its July 28–29 policy meeting on Wednesday Aug 19 at 2:00 p.m. ET. The Committee had left the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.50%–3.75% by a 9-3 vote — the most fractured decision in years — with three regional bank presidents dissenting in favor of an immediate 25bp increase. The minutes described an 'elevated' inflation backdrop with participants saying 'policy tightening would likely be necessary' if inflation did not decline.
explainer.howItWorks: The three dissenters were Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed's Neel Kashkari and Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan, each preferring to raise the target range by 25bp on price-stability grounds. Beyond the dissent, the minutes documented broad hawkish sentiment: participants debated whether AI-driven investment is shifting relative prices or fueling broader inflation, and flagged elevated asset valuations plus leverage in hedge funds as financial-stability concerns. Chair Kevin Warsh initiated a discussion of moving from eight FOMC meetings a year to six spaced roughly every two months, noting it 'would allow more information to accumulate between meetings' — no decision, and 2026's remaining meetings stay on the current calendar.
explainer.whyItMatters: The 9-3 vote and 'tightening would likely be necessary' language codify a hawkish skew that markets had been discounting only partially: it lowers the odds of a September cut and pushes the burden of proof onto the incoming CPI/jobs prints. Ironically, the equity reaction was muted (SPX +0.21% to 7,707.98) because the same afternoon Treasury Secretary Bessent doubled long-bond buybacks and yields fell; without that offset the read-through would have been more clearly negative for duration and long-duration equities. The Warsh cadence proposal is a structural signal — a six-meeting calendar would materially change how central-bank communication and market repricing work.
explainer.forWho: macro traders, rates desks, Fed watchers

3. **Financial stability** — 'elevated' asset valuations flagged, along with hedge-fund leverage and possible AI-sector repricing risk.
4. **Warsh's structural pitch** — Chair Kevin Warsh initiated a discussion of moving from 8 FOMC meetings a year to 6 (roughly every two months). No decision; 2026's remaining meetings stay on the current calendar.

What it means: September cut odds get harder to justify without a downside surprise in CPI or jobs. The muted equity reaction was almost entirely a Treasury-buyback-driven offset, not a dovish read of the minutes.

explainer.tagline: Bessent's Treasury doubles long-bond buyback caps to at least $4B a pop, lopping ~15bp off the 30Y yield and sinking the dollar in a surprise mid-quarter intervention.
explainer.whatIsIt: Two weeks after publishing its scheduled Q3 buyback calendar, the U.S. Treasury said on Wednesday Aug 19 it will 'at least double' the maximum size of its liquidity-support buyback operations for longer-dated nominal coupon securities. The new $4B-per-op cap (up from $2B) applies to the 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y sectors and takes effect Sept 9 through the Nov 4 quarterly refunding.
explainer.howItWorks: The action came less than 24 hours after the 30-year Treasury yield hit an intraday 5.337% on Tuesday — the highest since 2007 — with pressure driven by fiscal-deficit angst, sticky inflation and a wave of AI-capex investment-grade issuance clustered at the long end. Post-announcement the 30Y dropped ~15bp to 5.184%; the 10Y fell ~6bp to ~4.66%; and DXY had its biggest one-day drop in three weeks, sending gold ~+3.7% and silver above $65/oz. Bloomberg noted the total operations through the Nov 4 refunding could now aggregate roughly $83B. Sec. Bessent's move follows an Aug 1 U.S.-Japan yen intervention as his second market-support action this month.
explainer.whyItMatters: The size step-up — $4B per op is still small versus a ~$32T Treasury market — matters less as pure flow than as a signal that Treasury has drawn a line at the recent long-end selloff and is willing to move outside routine calendar operations to defend it. Rates traders now have to price in a de-facto ceiling under the 30Y while the Fed is still discussing whether it needs to hike; long-duration equities and TLT get a tailwind, the dollar an offset, and gold/silver a fresh bid. The move also plays with the July FOMC minutes released hours later — the Treasury effectively softened the hawkish read of the minutes on impact.

It also frames BABA's earlier-week Lingxi Games divestment as part of the same 'redirect cash to AI' pattern across the sector.

explainer.tagline: Klarna beat Q2 but cut its full-year volume and revenue outlook, and the stock got hammered on the German consumer read-through.
explainer.whatIsIt: Buy-now-pay-later fintech Klarna Group (NYSE: KLAR) reported Q2 2026 results and updated full-year guidance before the U.S. open on Aug 18. Q2 came in above consensus on both revenue and profitability, but the company trimmed its 2026 volume and revenue outlook, citing weaker consumer discretionary spending in Germany, its largest market by GMV.
explainer.howItWorks: Q2 revenue was $1.04B (+27% Y/Y) vs $996M est. Adjusted EPS was $0.01 vs a consensus loss of $0.06. GMV reached $36.6B (+18% Y/Y) and transaction-margin dollars were $446M (+42% Y/Y). For the full year, Klarna cut its GMV outlook to $149–151B (from a prior view above $155B) and revenue to $4.08–4.16B (from >$4.34B), attributing roughly $600M of the revenue cut to FX plus a 'more measured view of European volumes concentrated in Germany.' Management raised transaction-margin-dollar guidance to $1.62–1.65B — the framing: 'less business at better economics.'
explainer.whyItMatters: The German-consumer signal matters beyond KLAR itself: Germany is the euro area's largest economy and a bellwether for European discretionary spend. Read-across into other BNPL and euro-consumer names is negative, though PayPal and Affirm shrugged the print off on the view that Klarna's issue is geographic mix, not category demand. For KLAR shareholders it revives the post-IPO profitability-vs-growth debate that has kept the stock below its September 2025 $40 IPO price.

items.title: US 30-year Treasury yield tops 5.31% on Monday Aug 17 — highest since 2007 as debt-supply, sticky inflation and AI-capex issuance drive long-end selloff
items.summary: The 30-year US Treasury yield jumped ~6bp to 5.31% on Monday, its highest since 2007, on angst over surging deficits, inflation stuck above the Fed's 2% target and a wave of long-dated corporate AI-capex issuance.

explainer.tagline: 30Y Treasury yield hits 5.31% Monday, highest since 2007, as long-end sells off on deficits, inflation and AI-capex bond supply.
explainer.whatIsIt: The yield on the 30-year US Treasury climbed roughly six basis points on Monday Aug 17 to 5.31%, breaching last month's high and reaching the loftiest since 2007. Long-end government bond yields also rose in Canada (30Y highest since 2010) and Germany (rates at 2011 levels), reflecting a global reset in the price of long-dated debt.
explainer.howItWorks: The move steepens the curve: the 2Y is down about 12bp month-to-date while the 30Y is up 13bp, so the term premium is widening. Barclays strategist Anshul Pradhan said his desk continues to 'argue against fading the long-end selloff' and outlined a set of fiscal-and-issuance conditions that would need to break for a constructive turn. Drivers cited in coverage: mounting US government debt, inflation stuck above the Fed's 2% target for the past five years, waning demand from traditional long-bond buyers, and a fresh ramp of investment-grade issuance to fund AI capex.
explainer.whyItMatters: Rising real yields at the long end tighten financial conditions independently of the Fed's short-rate path — negative for long-duration equity (mega-cap tech, unprofitable growth, utilities) and for housing via 30Y mortgage rates. It also raises the Treasury's cost of funding a ~$2T deficit and puts pressure on the FOMC to justify near-term rate-cut expectations. 30Y closing above 5.44% would eclipse the 2007 GFC-era peak.
explainer.forWho: rates traders, macro, duration allocators

reddit.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5.31% — highest since 2007. Long-end selloff, curve steepening, AI-capex bond issuance takes some of the blame
reddit.body:
Monday Aug 17 the 30-year US Treasury yield rose ~6bp to 5.31%, the highest close since 2007. The 2007 peak of 5.44% is now the next test.

* 30Y yield: 5.31% intraday high, up ~6bp on the day
* 30Y MTD: +13bp; 2Y MTD: -12bp — curve is steepening
* Canada 30Y also hit its highest since 2010; German long rates at 2011 levels
* Fed's inflation target has been undershot for five straight years

The drivers cited in the coverage:

1. **Fiscal supply** — the Treasury is funding a giant deficit with more long-dated issuance and traditional real-money buyers are backing off.
2. **Sticky inflation** — five years of PCE above 2% is eroding faith in the 2% anchor; long-end investors want more term premium.
3. **AI-capex borrowing** — hyperscalers and their financing vehicles are pushing IG issuance sharply higher, tightening the crowding-out screw at the long end.

Barclays strategist Anshul Pradhan: 'We continue to argue against fading the long-end selloff.'

What it matters for: 30Y mortgage rates, long-duration equity multiples, and the FOMC's story on rate cuts into September.

Next catalysts: FOMC minutes later this week and Jackson Hole Aug 27–29.

items.summary: The NY Fed's Empire State factory index surged to 20.6 in August (vs 11.0 est, 15.6 July) — its strongest reading in more than four years — but prices paid jumped to 58.6 and delivery times worsened.

explainer.tagline: Empire State factory index leaps to 20.6 in August — a >4-year high — but prices paid at 58.6 keeps inflation risk alive.
explainer.whatIsIt: The New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Survey general business conditions index jumped to 20.6 in August 2026 from 15.6 in July, nearly doubling the median economist forecast of 11.0. NY Fed adviser Richard Deitz noted manufacturing activity 'increased at its fastest pace in over four years' — but with caveats.
explainer.howItWorks: Under the hood the picture is mixed: shipments cooled to 11.7 (from 24.4) and new orders eased to 17.3 (from 22.2), yet the unfilled-orders index jumped to 15.5 from 5.0 and delivery times lengthened to 20.6, signalling backlogs. Prices paid jumped to 58.6 from 52.3, its highest reading in a while, while prices received eased to 22.7. The forward six-month business-conditions index rose to 32.1 from 27.9.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the first regional Fed survey to land ahead of the September FOMC and it complicates the rate-cut story: real activity is hot AND input prices are re-accelerating just as the 30Y yield tops 5.31%. Watch the Philly Fed and manufacturing PMIs later this week — a matching hot print keeps the long end offered and shortens the dovish runway.
explainer.forWho: macro traders, rate desks

reddit.title: NY Empire State manufacturing surges to 20.6 in August (vs 11.0 est) — fastest pace in 4+ years, but prices paid rip to 58.6
reddit.body:
The first regional Fed manufacturing print for August landed hot — and inflation isn't dead in the sub-indices.

* Headline: 20.6 vs 11.0 est, prior 15.6 — strongest since spring 2022
* New orders: 17.3 (was 22.2)
* Shipments: 11.7 (was 24.4)
* Unfilled orders: 15.5 (was 5.0) — real backlog build
* Prices paid: 58.6 (was 52.3) — highest in a while
* Prices received: 22.7
* 6-month business conditions: 32.1 (was 27.9)

Two things to notice:

1. **Real activity is running hotter than expected** — NY Fed adviser Richard Deitz says manufacturing 'increased at its fastest pace in over four years,' with the caveat that delivery times worsened.
2. **Input prices are re-accelerating** — 58.6 on prices paid is a red flag for anyone modelling a September cut, and it lands on the same day the 30Y yield hit 5.31%.

items.title: Memory chip stocks rally Monday Aug 17 — Micron (MU) +5.8%, Western Digital (WDC) +5.4%, SanDisk (SNDK) +~5% after Commerce Sec Lutnick tells WSJ Trump admin opposes Apple buying Chinese memory (CXMT/YMTC)
items.summary: US memory stocks jumped Monday after Commerce Sec Howard Lutnick told the WSJ the Trump administration is 'not in favor' of Apple sourcing memory chips from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC — a de facto demand handoff to Micron, Samsung and SK hynix.

metrics.Source: WSJ interview with Commerce Sec Lutnick

explainer.tagline: Lutnick's 'not in favor' comment on Apple sourcing DRAM/NAND from CXMT and YMTC hands US memory names a demand tailwind.
explainer.whatIsIt: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told the Wall Street Journal that the Trump administration is 'not in favor' of Apple purchasing memory chips from Chinese suppliers ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT, DRAM) and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC, NAND). Apple had been testing CXMT DRAM and negotiating with YMTC for NAND, reportedly for products sold outside the US.
explainer.howItWorks: There is no formal rule or export order — Lutnick said he had told Apple 'plainly' — but the signalling was enough. Memory stocks jumped in Monday trading: Micron (MU) closed +5.8% near US$1,030, Western Digital (WDC) +5.4%, and SanDisk (SNDK) traded up ~5% after a ~10% premarket spike, on the read that Apple's memory dollars would flow to Micron, Samsung and SK hynix instead of Chinese suppliers. This lands on top of last week's SanDisk Investor Day (FY28–30 mid-to-high-teens revenue growth guide) and the July BofA Micron 'US 1' upgrade, both of which framed AI-driven NAND/DRAM tightness as structural.
explainer.whyItMatters: The US memory complex is already trading on AI-capacity tightness; an explicit Commerce Department nudge redirecting a mega-buyer like Apple hardens the demand base for MU, SNDK, WDC and SK hynix. Counterpoint: no rule = no legal enforcement, and CXMT/YMTC still supply the rest of the Android world. Watch for a formal export-control expansion at the next BIS window and any Apple statement pushing back on the framing.
explainer.forWho: semis, memory, AI-capex traders

Why it's more than one soundbite:

1. **Apple is a top-3 memory buyer globally** — redirecting even a slice of that demand to MU/Samsung/SK hynix meaningfully tightens an already tight market.
2. **Stacks on structural bull setup** — SNDK Investor Day (FY28-30 mid-to-high-teens rev growth) and BofA's Micron US-1 add all point to structural NAND/DRAM tightness through 2028.
3. **But — no rule = no enforcement** — Lutnick said he told Apple 'plainly' but there's no export order. Counterparty risk is a policy shift, not law.

BAC was cut and Constellation Brands exited — flags for defensive names that had been core positions.

items.title: Broadcom (AVGO) -5.94% to $392.99 on Friday Aug 14 after BofA's Tom Curcuruto flags AI-financing XPV vehicle could stack up to $370B of senior debt by mid-2029 at 20-GW scale; BofA cuts issuer + bond ratings but still lifts FY26 revenue and EBITDA estimates
items.summary: Broadcom -5.94% to $392.99 Friday after BofA analyst Tom Curcuruto warns the Apollo/Blackstone-led XPV chip-financing vehicle could pile up ~$370B of senior debt by mid-2029; issuer + bond ratings cut, but FY26 revenue/EBITDA estimates raised.

explainer.tagline: Bank of America's credit-side analyst turns cautious on Broadcom's off-balance-sheet AI-financing vehicle even as equity fundamentals stay strong.
explainer.whatIsIt: Bank of America credit analyst Tom Curcuruto published a note Friday Aug 14 downgrading Broadcom's issuer and bond ratings, focused on the AI XPV Platform Broadcom co-established with Apollo Global Management and Blackstone in June 2026. Curcuruto's model shows the vehicle could accumulate up to ~$370B of senior debt by mid-2029 at a 20-gigawatt scale — including roughly $150B of new issuance in 2027 alone. Shares of Broadcom fell 5.94% to $392.99, back below the $400 line, though BofA simultaneously raised its FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA estimates for AVGO.
explainer.howItWorks: The XPV Platform is an off-balance-sheet financing vehicle that raises third-party capital to buy custom AI accelerators and leases them to frontier AI labs. Apollo and Blackstone led a $35B initial financing in June 2026, and the first deployment funds more than 1 gigawatt of compute for Anthropic. Broadcom backstops customer lease payments for five years — capped at up to $29B on the initial tranche — while the platform is sized to support 20+ gigawatts through 2028. Curcuruto's $370B figure is the maximum senior-debt stack the vehicle would carry at 20 GW scale by mid-2029, not debt Broadcom itself would owe.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI-financing structures are now the primary transmission channel for the AI capex cycle — vehicles like XPV are what let hyperscalers and frontier labs finance GPU deployments off balance sheet, and they've been a tailwind for AVGO, APO, BX and NVDA. Curcuruto's note is the first credible sell-side pushback quantifying the debt trajectory. Broadcom itself is not on the hook for $370B, but the leverage math and the residual-value guarantees are what a downturn scenario would test. Watch Broadcom credit spreads and any read-through to Apollo/Blackstone private-credit vehicles.

FOXA rose 5.0% to $68.71. The upgrades cite Fox's fiscal-Q4 print from Aug 6 (revenue +28% Y/Y to $4.21B, adj EBITDA +27% to $1.20B), World Cup advertising tailwinds, and the pending $22B acquisition of Roku announced June 15.

items.summary: July U.S. CPI printed +0.1% M/M and +3.4% Y/Y with core +0.2% M/M and +2.5% Y/Y — both in line with LSEG consensus. Shelter (+0.1% M/M) was ~2/3 of the monthly gain, energy fell 1.5%.

explainer.tagline: In-line July CPI: headline 3.4% Y/Y, core down to 2.5% — cools the September-hike case a notch after last week's -23K payrolls.
explainer.whatIsIt: The BLS released the July 2026 Consumer Price Index at 8:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, Aug 12. Headline CPI rose 0.1% M/M and 3.4% Y/Y; core CPI (ex food & energy) rose 0.2% M/M and 2.5% Y/Y. Both readings matched the LSEG economist consensus.
explainer.howItWorks: Shelter accounted for roughly two-thirds of the monthly headline gain and rose 0.1% M/M. Energy prices fell 1.5% on the month, giving a meaningful drag on the headline number. Year-over-year, headline eased from June's 3.5% and core slipped from 2.6% — the second consecutive month of Y/Y deceleration on both series.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the final CPI print before Kevin Warsh's Sept 16–17 FOMC. Coming after last week's -23K July payrolls miss and a downward 103K revision to prior months, an in-line CPI takes some of the urgency out of the 'still-tight' argument for a September rate hike; markets went into the print with hike odds already sitting at ~44% versus 57% a week earlier. Shelter stickiness keeps core above the Fed's 2% target and prevents an outright dovish read.

Bloomberg reported the counterparty is Anthropic, the Claude maker. The disclosure landed alongside Riot's Q2 2026 print (revenue $174.2M +14% Y/Y, GAAP net loss $237.2M or -$0.68/share).
explainer.howItWorks: Riot will deliver 96 MW by December 2027 and complete the full 191 MW buildout by June 2028. The company estimates cumulative NOI of $7.3–$8.2B over the base term, or ~$365–$411M annually, with two five-year extension options that could raise the total contract value to ~$16.1B. Morgan Stanley provided a $573M interim financing facility to fund early construction while Riot works toward permanent credit arrangements. Combined with its existing 50 MW AMD contract, Riot now has 241 MW of AI-lease capacity signed.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is a step-change re-rating for Riot: bitcoin mining revenue ($113.7M in Q2, down Y/Y) is no longer the primary story — long-dated AI-lease cash flows are. It also validates the broader thesis that hyperscale AI labs are ready to buy power/space from anyone with a build-ready site, mirroring recent CoreWeave and neocloud deals. RIOT rallied ~25% in Monday's after-hours session and was up ~18% premarket Tuesday Aug 11, one of the largest single-session repricings among bitcoin miners this year.
explainer.forWho: AI-infrastructure allocators, bitcoin miner equity investors, power/data-center desks

explainer.tagline: eToro delivers a Q2 beat on funded accounts and adj. EPS and lines up TradeZero (~$80M revenue) for up to $231M to accelerate its U.S. active-trader push.
explainer.whatIsIt: eToro, the Nasdaq-listed multi-asset retail brokerage that IPO'd in May 2025 under 'ETOR', reported Q2 2026 results before the open Tuesday Aug 11 and simultaneously announced an agreement to acquire New York-based active-trader brokerage TradeZero for up to $231M. Company guidance for the deal: expected to close in 1H 2027, accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year post-close.
explainer.howItWorks: Q2 net contribution (eToro's proxy for net revenue after direct trading costs) grew 9% Y/Y to $229M, funded accounts rose 18% Y/Y to 4.28M, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.68 vs $0.56 in Q2 2025 (+21%). Assets under administration were $18.5B, down 5% Y/Y. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments stood at $1.2B on June 30, 2026. TradeZero — a direct-market-access, extended-hours-trading, stock-locate specialist for U.S. active traders — generated ~$80M in revenue at an ~81% gross margin in the twelve months ended June 30, 2026; its purchase adds broker-dealer infrastructure, proprietary trading platforms and operations in Canada. This is eToro's third acquisition signed this year (Zengo and Bit2C closed in Q2, focused on self-custody).
explainer.whyItMatters: The Q2 print confirms funded-account momentum and modest adj-EPS growth even with AUA down Y/Y on crypto price swings. Buying TradeZero is a straightforward tuck-in strategy to accelerate the U.S. build — CEO Yoni Assia called it 'a faster route to launching new products for U.S. customers' — and the target's ~81% gross margin means the deal shouldn't drag on unit economics if the price ($231M / ~$80M revenue = ~2.9x LTM sales) holds. Retail-broker peers Robinhood (HOOD) and Interactive Brokers (IBKR) trade at richer multiples on active-trader monetization.

items.title: Nvidia (NVDA) teams with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock (GIP), Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR on $500B AI infrastructure funding — NVDA -~3% Mon Aug 10 as ~$130B market cap wipes
items.summary: Nvidia and six of the largest Wall Street asset managers — Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock (via Global Infrastructure Partners), Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR — will mobilize more than $500B of third-party capital for hyperscalers, frontier labs and enterprises to fund data centers, power and NVDA hardware. NVDA fell ~3% Monday Aug 10 shedding roughly $130B of market cap.

explainer.tagline: Six of Wall Street's biggest asset managers will build a >$500B financing rail for AI infrastructure buyers of Nvidia hardware.
explainer.whatIsIt: Nvidia and a coalition of Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR will create dedicated pools of capital 'at significant scale at attractive rates for Nvidia customers,' per Financial Times reporting Monday Aug 10 that Bloomberg, CNBC, NBC News and Reuters corroborated. The package targets more than $500B of third-party capital for hyperscalers, frontier AI labs and enterprises to build data centers, power generation and buy Nvidia hardware.
explainer.howItWorks: The consortium extends previous AI-financing programs (e.g., Apollo/Blackstone's June $35B partnership with Broadcom for 20+ GW of compute) into a Nvidia-anchored rail across chips, energy and real assets. Jensen Huang told CNBC he approached only the six firms and none turned him down. Terms and timeline for individual deployments were not disclosed at publication; the six firms declined to comment or did not immediately respond to media requests.
explainer.whyItMatters: It formalizes the plumbing of AI capex — the private-credit / infra-fund complex now sits between Nvidia and its customer base, which lets buyers finance GPUs and data-center power instead of front-loading them on balance sheets. It also concentrates AI-infra risk in a handful of very large intermediaries, which several analysts flagged is 'reminiscent of 1999.' NVDA slid ~3% and shed ~$130B in market cap Monday as the market read the venture as a capex-demand hedge more than a demand pull.
explainer.forWho: AI-infrastructure allocators, private-credit desks, mega-cap semi investors

reddit.title: Nvidia + Apollo/Blackstone/BlackRock/Brookfield/Goldman/KKR to mobilize >$500B of AI-infra capital — NVDA -~3%, ~$130B market cap lost Monday Aug 10
reddit.body:
Nvidia is teaming with six of the biggest Wall Street asset managers to build a dedicated $500B+ financing rail for buyers of Nvidia hardware and the data centers/power that run them.

* Consortium: **Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock (Global Infrastructure Partners), Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR** — six firms Jensen Huang says he approached and none turned him down
* Target: **>$500B of third-party capital** for hyperscalers, frontier AI labs and enterprises
* Scope: chips, power generation and data centers
* NVDA reaction: **-~3% Monday**, shedding roughly **$130B in market cap**
* Builds on prior deals like Apollo + Blackstone's **June $35B** partnership with Broadcom for 20+ GW of compute

Two ways to read it:

1. **Capex demand pull** — private-credit + infra funds now sit between Nvidia and its customers, letting hyperscalers and enterprises finance GPUs and data-center power off balance sheet, which extends the AI capex cycle.
2. **Concentration risk hedge** — several analysts said the setup is 'reminiscent of 1999.' Financing the buyer of your product is exactly the kind of vendor-financed demand that can look great going up and ugly on the way down.

Next catalysts: July CPI Wed Aug 12, then CoreWeave (CRWV) earnings Mon Aug 11 AH and Cisco (CSCO) Aug 13.

items.summary: Intel announced a proposed $15B underwritten public offering of common stock Monday Aug 10, with a 30-day over-allotment for up to $2.25B of additional shares. J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citi lead the deal. INTC fell ~3.7% intraday on dilution then recovered to close at $101.65.

explainer.tagline: Intel taps public equity for a $15B common raise on Monday Aug 10 to fund its foundry and AI capex push.
explainer.whatIsIt: Intel priced a proposed $15B underwritten public offering of common stock Monday Aug 10 with a 30-day over-allotment option of up to $2.25B in additional shares. Proceeds are earmarked for 'general corporate purposes, which may include, but are not limited to, capital expenditures and working capital' as Intel bolsters its balance sheet ahead of continued fab and AI investment. J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citi are the joint book-running managers.
explainer.howItWorks: The offering is common stock (not preferred, not convertible), meaning immediate dilution rather than a debt overhang. Intel said the raise 'is intended to further enable Intel to pursue the growth opportunities ahead while maintaining a strong balance sheet and its commitment to an investment-grade rating.' The over-allotment (or 'greenshoe') can bring the total up to $17.25B if underwriters exercise it.
explainer.whyItMatters: It is the largest US-listed common-equity raise of the year and marks Intel management taking the dilution route to fund its foundry / AI-capex plan rather than issuing more debt. Shares slipped as low as $98.03 (-~3.7%) intraday on dilution fear before recovering to $101.65 on the close as buyers took the capital cushion as a de-risking event. The raise adds to a busy Intel financing tape that includes prior US-government stake and SoftBank-linked capital commitments in 2025-26.

explainer.tagline: Brent +5% to ~$87.72 Monday as the Iran/Oman handshake to reopen Hormuz slips past its expected date.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Iran/Oman diplomatic track that had brought Brent below $82 last week fell out of consensus over the weekend. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei also reshuffled the senior military ranks on Sunday, naming Ali Abdollahi armed-forces chief of staff and Ahmad Vahidi IRGC commander.
explainer.whyItMatters: It reprices Fed-cut math: higher energy costs feed into headline CPI (July print Wed Aug 12) and let Fed hawks argue a September hike stays live even after the July NFP miss. Energy majors caught a bid intraday but the broad Energy Select Sector ETF (XLE) still finished -1.2% on the day as the market read the move as a supply-shock risk premium (bad for demand) rather than a demand-led rally. items.summary: Bloomberg reports Monday Aug 10 that GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is weighing pulling the $56B unsolicited takeover offer for eBay and instead proposing a partnership/JV that would give eBay a physical retail footprint via GameStop's ~1,600 stores in exchange for board seats. GameStop still holds a 9.75% eBay stake (second-largest after Vanguard).

explainer.tagline: Cohen is reportedly ditching the takeover playbook for a JV plus board seats — the classic activist off-ramp when a bid gets rejected.
explainer.whatIsIt: Bloomberg reported Monday Aug 10 that GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is considering withdrawing the $56B unsolicited takeover offer he made for eBay in May 2026, and instead proposing a partnership or joint venture. Under the alternative, GameStop's ~1,600 US retail locations would give eBay a physical footprint in high-margin categories like trading cards and collectibles, and GameStop would seek seats on eBay's board.
explainer.howItWorks: The May bid was structured 50% cash / 50% GameStop common stock at $125/share; eBay's board rejected it as 'neither credible nor attractive.' Cohen escalated in July with a disclosed 9.75% eBay stake (second-largest holder after Vanguard funds). Bloomberg cites 'people familiar' and cautions no final decision has been made — Cohen retains other options. GameStop's spokesperson and eBay declined comment; PYMNTS, AOL, Quartz and Yahoo Finance ran matched coverage.
explainer.whyItMatters: It's the standard activist off-ramp when a full takeover stalls: convert the equity stake into board influence + a commercial JV that captures the strategic value without a proxy fight. Since the May bid, GME is -28% and EBAY is +7.6% (Fri close $111.98) — the arb tape had already written off the deal. If Cohen formalizes a JV in coming weeks, expect EBAY to trade on JV economics and GME to trade on collectibles-partner narrative rather than acquisition premium.

reddit.title: Rumor (Bloomberg): GameStop's Ryan Cohen weighing pulling the $56B eBay bid — JV using GME's ~1,600 stores + board seats is Plan B; GME still holds 9.75% of EBAY
reddit.body:
Bloomberg reported Monday Aug 10 that GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is considering **withdrawing** the $56B unsolicited takeover offer for eBay he tabled in May and pivoting to a partnership / JV instead.

* Original May bid: **$56B** — 50% cash / 50% GameStop common at **$125/share**
* eBay's board response (May): rejected as **'neither credible nor attractive'**
* GameStop stake in eBay disclosed **July 15: 9.75%** — 2nd-largest after Vanguard funds
* Since the bid: **GME -28%**, **EBAY +7.6%** (Fri close $111.98)

What Plan B looks like per Bloomberg's 'people familiar':

1. **JV / partnership** using GameStop's ~1,600 US stores as an eBay physical footprint in high-margin categories (trading cards, collectibles)
2. **Board seats** for GameStop as the negotiated concession
3. No final decision — Cohen keeps other options open

Why this is a normal off-ramp:

* The 9.75% stake becomes a board lever rather than an acquisition currency
* eBay avoids the fight and captures physical-retail economics without diluting shareholders
* The arb tape had already priced deal failure — GME is -28%, EBAY only +7.6%

This is a **rumor** — sourced to Bloomberg 'people familiar,' matched by PYMNTS, AOL, Quartz and Yahoo Finance. GameStop and eBay declined comment.

explainer.tagline: Ferguson beats on sales + EPS, raises FY26 sales-growth guide to mid-single-digit as non-residential capex holds up.
explainer.whatIsIt: Ferguson Enterprises — the largest US plumbing, HVAC, waterworks and industrial distributor and a recent S&P 500 add — reported Q2 FY26 (quarter ended June 30) before the open on Monday Aug 10 with both revenue and adjusted EPS ahead of Street estimates. Management also lifted full-year sales-growth guidance to the mid-single-digit range from prior 'low-to-mid single-digit'.
explainer.howItWorks: Sales came in at $8.8B, +4.6% Y/Y (est $8.68B); adjusted diluted EPS was $3.39 vs $3.30 est (+5.3% Y/Y) with GAAP EPS $3.43 (+6.9%). Gross margin was 31.0% (-20bp) but operating margin ticked up 10bp to 10.2% (10.7% adjusted). U.S. residential revenue was roughly flat while non-residential organic revenue grew 8% Y/Y on large capital projects (data centers, semis). Ferguson closed five acquisitions in the quarter and signed a definitive agreement to acquire FWI Holdings ('FloWorks'), taking year-to-date announced M&A to ~$1.4B of annualized revenue. It returned $202M via buybacks and declared a $0.89/share dividend; net debt/adjusted EBITDA sits at 1.3×.
explainer.whyItMatters: Ferguson is a proxy for U.S. non-residential construction: continued 8% non-res organic growth, driven by large capital projects, is another data point that AI-era data center and industrial capex is still underwriting the industrial-cyclical trade even with residential soft. The guide raise and FloWorks acquisition tightens the M&A roll-up story that lifted the stock into the S&P 500 last week. Shares traded up ~1.3% pre-market to ~$260 on the print.

items.summary: Barrick Q2 2026: adj EPS $0.82 (+74% Y/Y), revenue $5.29B, gold 796koz above guide; $1.21B buyback. Separately, Newmont pays $1.95B cash to expand Nevada Gold Mines JV into ~100M-oz complex and greenlights Barrick's North American IPO.

explainer.tagline: Barrick posts a beat-and-raise gold quarter and inks a $1.95B deal with Newmont that clears the runway for its North American IPO by year-end.
explainer.whatIsIt: Barrick Mining, the world's second-largest gold miner, released Q2 2026 results and — in a separate release the same morning — announced a comprehensive settlement with Newmont over their Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) joint venture. Both releases hit Monday Aug 10 pre-market.
explainer.howItWorks: Q2 revenue was $5.29B (+44% Y/Y) with adj EPS $0.82 (+74% Y/Y) and GAAP EPS $0.73 (+55%). Gold production of 796koz cleared 730-770koz guidance thanks to an ahead-of-schedule ramp at Loulo-Gounkoto and faster-than-expected Pueblo Viejo recovery; copper was 56kt (-5% Y/Y, in plan). Operating cash flow was $1.70B and the company returned $1.209B via buybacks under the $3.0B authorization plus a $0.175/share dividend. The Newmont deal has both sides vending in previously excluded properties — Barrick's Fourmile and Newmont's Fiberline and Mike developments — into NGM, creating a nearly 100M-oz gold reserve complex. Newmont pays Barrick a $1.95B cash top-up within 30 days, all outstanding NGM disputes are settled, and Newmont has consented to Barrick's proposed IPO of its North American gold assets.
explainer.whyItMatters: The Nevada deal ends a long-running JV standoff, hands Barrick $1.95B of dry-powder cash on top of a $1.2B/quarter buyback pace, and — critically — clears the last governance hurdle for the planned Barrick North American IPO by year-end 2026. On the earnings side, 796koz well above guide plus 74% Y/Y adj-EPS growth flags gold miners are still riding the ~$4,300/oz spot backdrop that lifted the group to multi-year highs. Newmont is the counterparty and pays the cash — expect the NEM read-through to be less clean than the B read-through.

items.title: Wendy's (WEN) Q2 FY26 — U.S. same-restaurant sales -7.0% (traffic -12.5%), 2026 outlook withdrawn, quarterly dividend halved to $0.07 ($0.28 annualized) as new CEO Bob Wright starts turnaround
items.summary: Q2 revenue $570.6M (+1.7% Y/Y) beat but U.S. comps -7.0% with traffic -12.5%, adj EBITDA $124.1M (-15.4% Y/Y), and adj EPS $0.18 (-37.9% Y/Y). Company pulled its 2026 outlook and cut the quarterly dividend in half to $0.07. Stock -2% Friday.

explainer.tagline: New CEO Bob Wright pulls guidance, halves dividend and cops to a broken value proposition after U.S. comps drop 7% on -12.5% traffic.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Wendy's Company reported Q2 2026 (quarter ended June 28) before market open Friday Aug 7. Revenue was $570.6M — up 1.7% Y/Y and above FactSet consensus — but every operating line was ugly. U.S. same-restaurant sales fell 7.0%, driven by a 12.5% traffic decline that a 5.6% higher average check couldn't offset. Adjusted EBITDA fell 15.4% Y/Y to $124.1M and adjusted diluted EPS dropped 37.9% to $0.18.
explainer.howItWorks: By segment, U.S. systemwide sales fell 8.2% and international rose 3.4% (comps -2.3% international, or +8.6% excluding weak Canada). Global systemwide sales dropped 6.5% in constant currency. New CEO Bob Wright — who joined from Charter Communications in July — said on the call that 'our traffic, our value proposition and franchisee economics are not meeting our expectations.' Wendy's simultaneously withdrew its 2026 financial outlook (previously calling for +2–3% systemwide sales growth) and cut the quarterly dividend to $0.07 from $0.14, taking the annualized rate to $0.28 from $0.56. The $0.07 dividend is payable Sept 15 to holders of record Sept 1. Management named five turnaround priorities: menu quality at competitive prices, demand-driving marketing, operational excellence, digital experience, and restaurant-driven growth.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the second Wendy's dividend cut in ~14 months (from $0.25 → $0.14 in mid-2025, now $0.14 → $0.07). Combined with the guide withdrawal and Wright's blunt language on unit economics, it reframes WEN from an income-and-value QSR story into a turnaround. Read-through to franchisee-heavy QSR peers — QSR/Burger King, JACK, YUM, MCD — on whether the traffic weakness is Wendy's-specific or category-wide (McDonald's Q2 U.S. comps of +1.3% earlier this week argue Wendy's-specific). The dividend cut also removes a significant leg of WEN's total-return case for yield holders.
explainer.forWho: consumer/QSR analysts, income investors, franchise-industry watchers

items.title: Silver +4.9% to $64.38/oz on Friday Aug 7 — six-week high on July jobs shock (-23K vs +80K est) as dollar drops and CTAs cover shorts; gold +1.8% to ~$4,342
items.summary: Spot silver ripped $3.00 (+4.9%) to $64.38/oz on Friday Aug 7 to a six-week high after July payrolls came in at -23K vs +80K est. Gold added ~1.8% to $4,341.94. SLV closed +2.2% at $57.09. Zerohedge/Goldman cited CTA short-cover plus dollar weakness.

explainer.tagline: The July payrolls miss + a soft dollar + light CTA positioning triggered silver's biggest single-day rally in weeks.
explainer.whatIsIt: Spot silver rallied 4.9% to $64.38/oz on Friday Aug 7 to a six-week high, alongside a 1.8% move in gold to roughly $4,341.94/oz. The trigger was the BLS morning print showing U.S. nonfarm payrolls fell 23K in July versus consensus of +80K, and combined May+June revisions -103K. iShares Silver Trust (SLV) closed +2.2% at $57.09.
explainer.howItWorks: Zerohedge and Goldman flagged the mechanics: Managed Money net length was only a 3% two-year rank on July 28, so positioning was extremely light heading into the jobs data. Once the print hit, CTAs covered shorts and front-ran the trend, layered on top of a 1.7% DXY drop between July 28 and Aug 5 and continued physical demand from London. Silver's move outpaced gold, tightening the gold-silver ratio to roughly 67 from ~69 a week earlier.
explainer.whyItMatters: The weak jobs print reset Fed-path expectations — September rate-hike odds slid to ~44% from 57% pre-print — which mechanically pressured real yields and the dollar and boosted both metals. The unusually light CTA positioning (3% two-year rank) turned an otherwise-normal macro move into an outsized 5% single-session pop in silver. Read-through: broader precious-metals miners (SIL, GDX), FCX and silver-heavy names like PAAS, WPM, FSM saw sympathy bids. The move puts silver back within striking distance of its record from earlier this year.

items.title: Trump Media (DJT), Crypto.com and Yorkville mutually terminate ~$6.42B 'Trump Media Group CRO Strategy' SPAC on Friday Aug 7 — plus Truth Social prediction-market integration and Crypto.com ETF servicing agreement scrapped; CRO -6% to $0.05009 (lowest since 2023)
items.summary: Trump Media, Crypto.com and Yorkville Acquisition mutually killed the $6.42B CRO treasury SPAC (plus a Truth Social prediction-market tie-up and an ETF servicing pact) on Friday Aug 7, citing 'prevailing market conditions' and shifting priorities. CRO fell 6% to $0.05009, its lowest since 2023.

explainer.tagline: $6.42B Trump Media–Crypto.com CRO treasury SPAC dies; CRO -6% to a 2023 low as three planned tie-ups all get scrapped.
explainer.whatIsIt: Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ: DJT), Crypto.com and Yorkville Acquisition Corp. filed an 8-K on Friday Aug 7, 2026 disclosing they had signed a Mutual Termination and Release Agreement ending the previously announced business combination that would have created 'Trump Media Group CRO Strategy, Inc.' The originally announced funding package around the SPAC was reported at ~$6.42B, structured as $1B of CRO tokens, $200M cash, warrants, and a $5B credit line. Two related tie-ups — a Crypto.com ETF servicing agreement for Yorkville America ETFs and a Truth Social prediction-market integration — were also scrapped in the same filing.
explainer.howItWorks: The 8-K classifies the termination under Item 1.02 (material termination of a definitive agreement) and states that 'all initial discussions and development efforts regarding the proposed business combination and digital asset treasury structure' will cease. Yorkville America's existing and future ETF offerings remain unchanged; the ETF servicing partnership with Crypto.com is what was terminated. Interim CEO Kevin McGurn told Axios the pivot reflects a saturated digital-asset-treasury market and a shift toward media, data licensing and finalizing DJT's proposed merger with fusion-energy firm TAE Technologies. Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek said: 'moving forward under current market conditions doesn't make sense.'
explainer.whyItMatters: CRO fell ~6% to $0.05009 — the token's lowest level since 2023 — as the anticipated $1B CRO purchase from the treasury vehicle evaporates. The termination is the most concrete sign yet that the 2024-25 wave of publicly-traded digital-asset-treasury (DAT) SPAC vehicles has stalled amid falling premiums, tighter capital-markets conditions and heightened ethics scrutiny around the Trump family's crypto ventures. Trump Media still holds ~9,542 BTC (~$600M at recent prices) on its balance sheet, so DJT retains material crypto exposure — but its ambition to become a diversified DAT operator is off the table.
explainer.forWho: crypto desks, DAT-SPAC arb funds, DJT holders

items.summary: Berkshire posted Q2 operating earnings $12.98B (+16.3% Y/Y) and — per the 10-Q — was a net buyer of stocks for the first time in 14 quarters, purchasing ~$20B more in equities than sold. Cash pile fell to $365.5B from Q1's record $397.4B; buybacks ran $4.5B, ~19x Q1's $235M.

metrics.Net stock purchases: ~$20B (first net-buyer quarter in 14; prior streak of net selling)

explainer.tagline: In his second quarter as CEO, Greg Abel ended Berkshire's 14-quarter selling streak, deploying ~$32B of cash into stock and buybacks.
explainer.whatIsIt: Berkshire Hathaway published Q2 2026 results on Saturday Aug 8 alongside its 10-Q. Net earnings attributable to shareholders were $25.67B, more than double last year's $12.37B, boosted by a $12.68B swing in investment gains on the equity book. Operating earnings — Berkshire's own preferred measure — rose to $12.98B from $11.16B a year earlier.
explainer.howItWorks: The 10-Q's capital-allocation lines are the story. Berkshire was a net buyer of equities for the first time in 14 quarters, purchasing roughly $20B more in stock than it sold, and repurchased ~$4.5B of its own shares (six-month total ~$4.8B; Q1 was just ~$235M). The combined outflow drew the cash-and-Treasuries pile from a record $397.4B at Q1 down to $365.5B at June 30 — a $31.9B decline. Segment breakout: insurance-underwriting $1.73B (down from $1.99B), insurance-investment income $3.06B, BNSF $1.56B, Berkshire Hathaway Energy $891M (+27% Y/Y), manufacturing/service/retailing $4.47B (+24% Y/Y). 'Other' jumped to $1.27B on $326M of FX gains from non-USD debt. Insurance float ticked up to $177.5B from $176.4B at year-end 2025.
explainer.whyItMatters: The shift is what watchers have been waiting for since Buffett handed over on Jan 1. Berkshire had been a net seller of stocks for 14 straight quarters — one of the longest such stretches in company history — while the cash pile grew every quarter. Ending both streaks in the same quarter, with a $32B cash drawdown and a $4.5B buyback (the largest since Q1 2021), is the clearest signal yet that Abel views current prices as attractive. A separately-disclosed $10B private placement in Alphabet (announced June 1) is inside the Q2 window; the balance of what Berkshire bought becomes visible in the Aug 14 13F filing.
explainer.forWho: large-cap value investors, Berkshire watchers

* Cash + Treasuries fell to **$365.5B** from Q1's record $397.4B (a $31.9B drawdown)

2. **The cash pile finally moves** — after 14 quarters of hoarding cash to a record $397.4B, Abel drew it down $32B in a single quarter. Direction matters more than magnitude.
3. **Segments look clean** — BHE +27% Y/Y to $891M, manufacturing/services/retailing +24% to $4.47B, BNSF +6%. Insurance underwriting the one soft spot at $1.73B (down from $1.99B).

Next catalyst: the Aug 14 13F filing reveals which stocks Berkshire bought beyond the already-disclosed $10B Alphabet private placement.

items.title: U.S. July 2026 jobs report — nonfarm payrolls -23K (first monthly loss since 2020) vs +80K est; May and June combined revised DOWN 103K; unemployment 4.1% only because participation slipped; S&P 500 to record 7,757.64 as September Fed hike odds slide 57% → 44%
items.summary: BLS July NFP -23K vs +80K est — the first monthly decline since December 2020. Prior two months revised -103K combined; unemployment 4.1% (-0.1pp) as participation drops; wages +3.2% Y/Y (lowest since May 2021). S&P +0.62% record close 7,757.64, 10Y -6bp to ~4.62%.

explainer.tagline: BLS July jobs prints the first negative payrolls month since 2020, with combined May+June revisions of -103K — S&P sets a fresh record and the market yanks September Fed-hike odds sharply lower.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' July 2026 Employment Situation, released 8:30 a.m. ET Friday August 7, showed nonfarm payrolls declined by 23,000 versus the Dow Jones +80K consensus — the first monthly loss since December 2020. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% from 4.2%, but for the 'wrong' reason: labor force participation slipped as workers left the job market. Prior two months lost a combined 103K in revisions.
explainer.howItWorks: May was revised to +63K (from +129K) and June to +20K (from +57K). Losses were led by local government education (-50K), leisure & hospitality (-40K), retail trade (-19K) and financial activities (-14K); healthcare (+22K) and professional & business services (+18K) contributed the meaningful gains. Average hourly earnings rose 3.2% year-over-year — the softest wage pace since May 2021. Reaction was immediate: the 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to roughly 4.62%, the S&P 500 closed at a fresh record 7,757.64 (+0.62%), the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.30% to 26,690.62, and the Dow added 0.28% to 54,036.93. For the week the S&P rose ~3.5% and the Nasdaq ~5.0%, the best week since April. Rate-futures markets cut the probability of a September Fed hike to 43.9% from 57% just before the release; a hold now prices at 60.4%.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the cleanest labor-side data point yet against Chair Warsh's hawkish tilt. The Fed has been dissenting toward hikes to slow sticky services inflation, but a negative payrolls print with 103K of downward revisions puts the labor-market pillar of that case under stress. Front-end rates and rate-sensitive equities (regional banks, homebuilders, small caps) rallied on the shape of the print. Next week's CPI (August 13) is now the swing variable — a firm print keeps hikes on the table; a cool print flips the base case toward cuts, which Citi already forecasts for October.

explainer.tagline: One of the largest lockup expirations in history: ~$116B of SpaceX insider shares become tradeable Thursday.
explainer.whatIsIt: SpaceX went with a staggered lockup rather than a single 180-day cliff. The first — and largest — tranche expires Thursday Aug 6, 2026, freeing up to 20% of eligible insider shares (about 911.5M shares) to trade. At the Aug 5 close of $108.27, that is roughly $99B; at ~$127 (the Motley Fool's mark) it's closer to $116B. Elon Musk's ~6.4B shares stay locked until June 12, 2027.
explainer.howItWorks: A second tranche of 455.8M shares was designed to release early if SPCX traded at ≥30% above the $135 IPO price on 5 of any 10 sessions (above ~$175.50). That didn't happen — SPCX is 42% off its June 16 intraday high of $225.64 and below the IPO price — so that tranche stays locked. Full expiry for the rest of the block is Dec 8, 2026. SPCX was down ~4% in the days leading up to the unlock as market makers hedged for supply.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is a live float roughly 2.4× overnight. Two scenarios: insiders sell aggressively into weak sentiment (deepens the drawdown) or they hold and the technical overhang fades over the next 2–3 weeks. Morgan Stanley called current levels an 'attractive entry point' — implicitly arguing the sell-side has already priced the unlock. Options desks will watch skew and 30-day IV into next week's tape.

Antitrust lawyer Andre Barlow told AOL/Reuters he expects the Trump FTC to scrutinize the combination given significant overlap in cancer immunotherapy franchises — likely requiring divestitures similar to BMY's $13.4B Otezla sale during the Celgene deal.

A megadeal at this size would be the largest pharma M&A ever and reset the sector's consolidation calculus after years of frozen dealmaking on antitrust and drug-pricing concerns.

explainer.tagline: Alibaba flips Qwen3.8-Max from July 19 WAIC preview to broad availability + open-weights next week — HK:9988 +7%, BABA ADR +4.7% premarket.

explainer.tagline: Trump calls off Iran strike he ordered Friday, says deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz has agreed 'perimeters.'
explainer.whatIsIt: Late Saturday August 1 Trump posted on Truth Social that he had cancelled a planned US military attack on Iran after allies asked him to hold off, saying 'perimeters of a deal' have been agreed. The proposed framework calls for the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT' and 'an end to Iran's nuclear threat.' It reverses the WSJ-reported Friday order to attack Iran as soon as this weekend that had lifted WTI above $86 in post-settlement trade.
explainer.howItWorks: Trump wrote he had 'agreed, for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL,' adding that 'The country of Israel joins me in this commitment.' Saudi Crown Prince MBS spoke with Trump at 4:54 AM EDT urging de-escalation. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held calls with Pakistani, Turkish and Saudi officials while stressing Iran will respond 'proportionately' if strikes resume; Iranian state media declined to corroborate that a deal has been agreed.
explainer.whyItMatters: If the deal holds, the Hormuz reopening would reverse the shipping-lane closure Iran imposed March 4 that pushed Brent to $101 on July 23 and drove Q2 CPI/PCE back above 3%. Immediate market impact plays out at Sunday-night oil futures open and Monday cash equities: energy names (XOM, CVX, SLB) that just posted record Iran-war Q2s become the swing trade, defence primes (LMT) give back some of the recent bid, and the dollar/yen bid on safe-haven flows likely fades. explainer.tagline: The Fed's preferred wage gauge cools less than expected as real wages for private workers fall for the first time in four years.
explainer.whatIsIt: The BLS released the Q2 2026 Employment Cost Index Friday July 31. Total civilian compensation rose 0.9% Q/Q seasonally adjusted, one tick above the +0.8% Bloomberg consensus, and 3.4% Y/Y over the four quarters ending June.

The headline surprise is beneath the nominal print: real, inflation-adjusted wages and salaries for private-sector workers fell 0.4% Y/Y — the first Y/Y decline since 2022 — because Iran-conflict energy prices pushed CPI higher through Q2 even as nominal wage growth cooled.
explainer.whyItMatters: ECI is the Fed's preferred wage measure precisely because it's mix-adjusted, so a hotter-than-expected print reduces the case for the Fed's current hold-through-year-end stance and stiffens the resolve of the Hammack/Kashkari/Logan hike-dissent camp seen at the July 29 FOMC. Real-wage decline complicates the political calculus for Fed Chair Warsh; it's also a consumer-spending headwind that feeds into softer big-ticket demand.

explainer.tagline: Fed's preferred inflation gauge cools sharply on the headline in June — but core PCE stays sticky at 3.3%, extending the longest above-3.3% run since 2023.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Bureau of Economic Analysis published the June 2026 Personal Income and Outlays report on Thursday July 30. Headline PCE fell 0.1% M/M and dropped to +3.7% Y/Y (from +4.1% in May), the biggest month-over-month drop in the headline in some time. Core PCE — which strips out food and energy and is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.1% M/M and eased to +3.3% Y/Y (from +3.4% in May).
explainer.howItWorks: Headline PCE benefited from lower energy prices in June. Core PCE at +3.3% has now been at or above that level for four straight months — the longest such streak since the fall of 2023. The report lands the day after the FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 hawkish-dissent vote, with three members (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) pushing for a 25bp hike. The June print doesn't materially shift the case for either side of that debate: headline cooled, core stayed sticky.
explainer.whyItMatters: The 40bp drop in headline PCE gives the Fed's doves a talking point, but sticky core keeps the hawks' case alive — the setup that produced Wednesday's 3-dissent hold. Fed funds futures pricing barely moved on the print. Markets are now looking to August 1 nonfarm payrolls and the August 26 next PCE release as the next inflection points on the September FOMC path.

items.summary: Fed holds federal funds range at 3.50-3.75% for fifth straight meeting on 9-3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented for +25bp. Warsh press conference: 'no soft inflation target'. Dow -1,153 pts (-2.19%), 30Y +12bp to 5.21%.

explainer.tagline: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote as three regional presidents dissent for a hike and long-end yields spike to a 19-year high.
explainer.whatIsIt: The FOMC voted 9-3 on Wednesday July 29 to keep the federal funds target range at 3.50-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting. Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis' Neel Kashkari and Dallas' Lorie Logan dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference doubled down on his 'no soft inflation target' framing.
explainer.howItWorks: The statement kept the language that economic activity is 'expanding at a solid pace' while flagging inflation as 'elevated' relative to the 2% goal. Three dissents on a hold is the biggest hawkish split at an FOMC since 2019. Warsh reiterated the Fed 'will deliver price stability' and pushed back on giving forward guidance, urging markets to trade the data rather than Fed policy.
explainer.whyItMatters: The Dow dropped 1,153.18 points (-2.19%) to 51,594.14 for its worst session since April 2025 as traders read the three dissents and Warsh's 'no soft target' rhetoric as confirmation the next move is a hike, not a cut. The 30-year yield surged 12bp to 5.21%, its highest since 2007, and the 10-year jumped 7bp to 4.67%. S&P -1.52% to 7,316.15; Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,442.94.
explainer.forWho: rates traders, macro allocators, duration desks

reddit.title: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% on 9-3 vote as Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissent for a hike — Dow -1,153 pts (-2.19%), 30Y yield spikes to 5.21%, highest since 2007
reddit.body:
Warsh's second FOMC as chair delivered a hawkish hold. The market did not like it.

* Fed funds range unchanged at 3.50-3.75% for the 5th straight meeting
* Vote 9-3 — Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis) and Lorie Logan (Dallas) all dissented in favor of a 25bp HIKE
* Statement says inflation 'remains elevated' vs the 2% goal, economy still 'expanding at a solid pace'
* Warsh presser: 'There is no soft inflation target. There's only a target, and it's 2%'

Market reaction was ugly:

1. **Dow -1,153.18 pts (-2.19%)** to 51,594.14 — worst day since April 2025
2. **S&P 500 -1.52%** to 7,316.15 / **Nasdaq -1.74%** to 24,442.94
3. **Long end spikes** — 30Y yield +12bp to 5.21%, the highest since 2007; 10Y +7bp to 4.67%

Bond market read: three dissents plus Warsh's 'no soft target' framing = next move is a hike, not a cut.

Next catalysts: Q2 GDP advance estimate Thursday July 30 (8:30 AM ET), then AAPL/AMZN after the close.

explainer.tagline: Boeing beats on revenue and delivers record $715B backlog and +$0.6B FCF, but a fresh $280M Air Force One charge sends core loss to ($0.76).
explainer.whatIsIt: The Boeing Company reported Q2 2026 results before the open Tuesday July 28. Revenue rose 8% to $24.6B, deliveries hit 171 (highest since 2018) and free cash flow flipped positive at +$0.6B versus a $0.2B outflow a year earlier. But the Defense unit took another $280M loss on the VC-25B (Air Force One) program.

GAAP net loss was $428M (vs $612M Y/Y) or ($0.67)/sh; core loss per share widened to ($0.76) vs a Street ($0.31) estimate.
explainer.whyItMatters: Two Boeings visible in one print: the operational turnaround (record backlog, cash back to positive, delivery cadence rebuilding to pre-2019 levels) is progressing, but the fixed-price defense programs — VC-25B, KC-46, T-7A, MQ-25 — keep grinding out charges that leak into headline EPS. Investors focused on the FCF inflection and the $597B commercial backlog on 6,200+ jets rather than the bottom-line miss.

Boeing dropped Q2 before the open Tuesday. Revenue beat, cash flow flipped positive, deliveries hit a 2018 high — and defense fixed-price programs bit again.

* Core loss per share ($0.76) vs ($0.31) est
* GAAP net loss $428M (vs $612M loss Y/Y)

3. **Cash inflection is the story** — first positive FCF quarter in a while, ops cash $1.4B, backlog at all-time high; the market gave Boeing the benefit of the doubt on the EPS miss.

explainer.whatIsIt: SanDisk (SNDK) was the Russell 1000's worst performer on Monday July 27, 2026, dropping about 11.7% intraday and settling near $1,268. The session low of $1,222.01 was the stock's weakest print since early May, extending losses to roughly 45% from the June record of $2,354.39.
explainer.howItWorks: The catalyst was the +466% Shanghai STAR debut of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) — mainland China's biggest IPO since 2010 and a signal that Chinese DRAM/NAND capacity is scaling faster than US memory names had priced. Friday July 24 already saw SNDK -10.8% on the Korean chip sell-off; Monday's leg extended the rout on the same theme.
explainer.whyItMatters: SanDisk is the pure-play NAND expression in the US large-cap complex, so it takes the sharpest edge of any China-supply shock. The Aug 5 SNDK earnings print now becomes the referendum on how much of the sell-off is China-competition vs. AI-capex fatigue. Also on the tape: Micron (MU) held up better on HBM exposure, keeping the pair-trade alive.
