items.title: CrowdStrike Q1 FY27 — record $256M net new ARR (+32% Y/Y), $5.51B ARR, non-GAAP EPS $1.10 beat; raises FY27 revenue guide to $5.92–5.96B and announces 4-for-1 stock split (record June 25, trades split-adjusted July 2); CRWD ~-9% AH on June 3
items.summary: CrowdStrike Q1 FY27 beat ($1.39B revenue +26%, EPS $1.10 vs $1.07 est, $256M record net new ARR) and raised FY27 to $5.92–5.96B; 4-for-1 split takes effect July 2, but CRWD drops ~9% AH on valuation reset.

explainer.tagline: Record net new ARR, raised guide and a 4-for-1 split — but CRWD slips ~9% AH on valuation after a 40% rally off the April lows.
explainer.whatIsIt: CrowdStrike posted Q1 FY27 (quarter ended April 30, 2026) after the close on Wednesday June 3. Revenue was $1.39B (+26% Y/Y), subscription $1.32B (+26%), and non-GAAP EPS $1.10 (+15%) topped the $1.07 consensus.
explainer.howItWorks: Ending ARR reached $5.51B (+24% Y/Y) with a record Q1 net new ARR of $256M (+32%). FY27 revenue guide raised to $5.92–5.96B from $5.87–5.93B and non-GAAP EPS to $4.88–4.96 from $4.78–4.90. explainer.howItWorks: The raise has three legs: $30B in concurrent underwritten public offerings of Class A common ($355.20), Class C capital stock ($351.80), and Series A/B depositary shares for 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred ($50 each); a $40B at-the-market program selling shares directly into the open market over time; and a $10B private placement to Berkshire Hathaway. The total $4.75B upsize from the original $80B headline reflects strong order books.

GOOGL fell ~3.5% at the June 2 open on dilution math and the ATM creates a steady supply overhang. items.summary: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Kuwait International Airport (1 dead, 63 injured) and at Bahrain (intercepted) at dawn June 3. U.S. responds with strikes on Iranian ground-control station on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

metrics.Iran missiles fired at Kuwait: 2 (fell short / disintegrated; drone separately struck airport)
metrics.U.S. response: Strike on Iranian ground-control station, Qeshm Island

explainer.tagline: Iran missiles hit Kuwait's main airport and target Bahrain at dawn June 3; U.S. responds with new strikes on Qeshm Island.
explainer.whatIsIt: At dawn on June 3, 2026 Iran launched several ballistic missiles toward Gulf neighbors — two toward Kuwait that fell short or disintegrated, and three toward Bahrain that U.S. and Bahraini air defenses intercepted. A separate Iranian drone struck Kuwait International Airport, killing one person and injuring at least 63 including airport workers and passengers.
explainer.howItWorks: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry condemned the attack and confirmed damage to terminal infrastructure. In response, U.S. CENTCOM launched strikes on an Iranian military ground-control station on Qeshm Island, which sits inside the Strait of Hormuz. The exchange comes after Iran reportedly suspended communications with mediators over an extension of the May ceasefire framework.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the first directly attributable Iranian strike on civilian Gulf airport infrastructure in this round, and the highest-casualty incident in the post-truce escalation cycle. The Qeshm strike escalates the U.S. footprint inside the Hormuz chokepoint; ~20% of global oil and most Qatari LNG transits Hormuz. Risk-off bid in Treasuries and a fresh bid in WTI/Brent (oil already +5–6% Monday) are the immediate transmission channels.

explainer.tagline: Goldman halves its Intuit price target and goes outright Sell on AI tax-prep disruption.
explainer.whatIsIt: Goldman Sachs downgraded Intuit from Neutral to Sell on June 2 and slashed its 12-month price target to $276 from $519, citing rising competitive threats from AI-powered tax-preparation entrants. INTU traded ~-6% in premarket.
explainer.howItWorks: Goldman flagged TurboTax — about 25% of Intuit's revenue and operating income — as the most exposed product. The bank pointed to Prime Meridian, Perplexity Tax and Chime Tax, arguing AI models can process tax returns at near-zero marginal cost versus TurboTax's ~$162 average revenue per return. Goldman reset valuation to 15x GAAP earnings, reflecting a shift from a 14% historical long-term revenue CAGR toward a 5–10% range.

It is one of the cleanest Street statements that AI tooling is now compressing the moats of legacy workflow SaaS — read-through to ADBE, ADP and CRM as the next debates.

Lago had been Nubank's CFO through the IPO and the company's expansion into Mexico, Colombia and the U.S.; the change lands as Nubank is moving into U.S. consumer banking, where Livingston's North American credit-card and payments background is more directly relevant. items.summary: HPE smashed Q2 FY26: revenue $10.68B (+40%) and non-GAAP EPS $0.79 vs $0.54 est, with Networking $2.7B (+148%) reflecting Juniper. FY26 EPS guide lifted to $3.35–$3.45; HPE +9.35% close, ~+30% AH.

explainer.tagline: HPE delivers biggest earnings beat since 2018 as Juniper integration runs ahead of schedule and AI server orders nearly double.
explainer.whatIsIt: Hewlett Packard Enterprise posted fiscal Q2 2026 results after the close on June 1, 2026, with revenue and adjusted EPS both blowing past Street estimates. The company also raised its full-year guidance by a wide margin, with the prior FY26 non-GAAP EPS range of $2.30–$2.50 replaced by $3.35–$3.45.
explainer.howItWorks: Total revenue hit $10.68B versus the ~$9.79B consensus and FY26 outlook is now 29–33% revenue growth. Networking revenue more than doubled to $2.7B (+148% Y/Y) on the recently closed Juniper Networks acquisition, while Server revenue jumped 33% to $5.5B as AI orders and AI backlog nearly doubled Y/Y. explainer.whyItMatters: The print is HPE's biggest earnings beat since 2018 and confirms that Juniper synergies are landing faster than the integration plan. HPE closed regular trading +9.35% at $47.06 before adding roughly 30% in after-hours trade, extending Friday's sympathy rally on Dell's AI-server blowout. AI-server peers Dell, Supermicro and Pure Storage trade off this read.

items.title: U.S. ISM Manufacturing PMI for May 2026 jumps to 54.0% — highest reading since May 2022; New Orders 56.8, Production 54.3, Prices 82.1 as 19-month expansion streak continues
items.summary: ISM Manufacturing PMI prints 54.0% in May (vs 52.7% in April), the highest since May 2022. New Orders accelerate to 56.8 and Prices stay hot at 82.1; ISM says reading maps to ~2.2% annualized GDP growth.

explainer.tagline: U.S. manufacturing logs its fastest expansion in three years with New Orders accelerating and Prices Paid still in the 80s.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Institute for Supply Management released its May 2026 Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 a.m. ET on June 1, 2026. The headline came in at 54.0%, 1.3 percentage points above April and the highest reading since May 2022's 55.9.
explainer.howItWorks: New Orders rose 2.7 ppt to 56.8, Production added 0.9 ppt to 54.3 and Employment climbed 2.2 ppt but stayed sub-50 at 48.6 — the 32nd straight contractionary print for factory hiring. Prices Paid eased 2.5 ppt to 82.1 but remain elevated as tariffs and steel/aluminum costs push input prices. ISM Chair Susan Spence noted the 54.0 reading corresponds to roughly 2.2% annualized real GDP growth.
explainer.whyItMatters: A re-acceleration in factory activity alongside still-hot Prices Paid complicates the Warsh Fed's first meeting on June 16–17. With the 10Y already pinned above 5% on inflation worries and core PCE running +3.3% Y/Y, sticky goods-side prices keep an early rate cut off the table.
explainer.forWho: Macro traders, rates desks, industrial-equity analysts.

Mid-single-digit organic growth plus margin leverage drive the base case, with a $449 bull case sized off quantum becoming a real revenue line. IBM closed roughly 6% higher in regular trading, extending a one-month run of around 28%.

explainer.tagline: Salesforce buys headless CMS Contentful to give Agentforce a real content layer — and CRM rides the broader software re-rating.

Salesforce frames the move as removing 'content fragmentation' as a bottleneck for agentic AI workflows. The announcement landed on the same day NVIDIA's Computex keynote re-rated the software complex, sending CRM up roughly 9.7%, IBM ~+6%, ServiceNow ~+9% and Adobe ~+6.6%.

items.title: NVIDIA unveils RTX Spark — 1 PFLOP Arm-based Windows PC superchip co-built with Microsoft and MediaTek — at Computex on May 31; NVDA +~3.9%, MSFT +~3.1%, INTC -~6.3% on Monday June 1
items.summary: Jensen Huang's Computex keynote unveiled RTX Spark — a Blackwell RTX GPU + 20-core NVIDIA Grace ARM CPU + MediaTek superchip running Windows for Arm. Touts 1 petaflop AI compute, 6,144 RTX cores and up to 128GB unified memory. Launch partners: Microsoft Surface, Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo and MSI in fall 2026. INTC -6.3% on the threat to x86 laptops.

explainer.tagline: NVIDIA enters the Windows laptop CPU market with a 1 petaflop Arm superchip co-developed with Microsoft and MediaTek.
explainer.whatIsIt: At Computex 2026 in Taipei on May 31, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang unveiled RTX Spark, an Arm-based PC superchip combining a Blackwell RTX GPU with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU and MediaTek-co-designed silicon. Microsoft is positioning Windows for Arm as the runtime. First laptops ship in fall 2026 from Microsoft Surface, Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo and MSI (Acer and GIGABYTE to follow).
explainer.howItWorks: RTX Spark delivers 1 petaflop of AI compute with fifth-generation Tensor Cores and FP4 precision. The 6,144-core Blackwell RTX block pairs with a 20-core Grace CPU and up to 128GB unified memory — enough to run 120-billion-parameter language models with a million-token context, edit 12K video, or render 90GB+ scenes locally. Huang's framing: 'For forty years, you launched apps. With RTX Spark and Microsoft Windows, you ask — and the PC does the work.'
explainer.whyItMatters: Drops NVIDIA into the PC CPU market long owned by Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Apple — and reinforces Microsoft's bet on Windows for Arm. INTC fell ~6.3% on the day as the Street priced in lost premium-laptop share; MSFT gained ~3.1% on the Surface/AI-PC tailwind; NVDA added ~3.9% on top of the data-center franchise. The roadmap is also a clear win for MediaTek's CPU IP and ARM's PC ambitions versus x86.

WTI +~6% to ~$92, Brent +~5% to ~$95. Defense Secretary Hegseth said the US would resume Iran strikes if negotiations collapse.

metrics.Context: Brent fell ~19% in May on Iran-deal optimism

explainer.tagline: Crude snaps back: Brent +~5%, WTI +~6% Monday as Iran's Tasnim flags a talks halt and Israel expands its Lebanon offensive.
explainer.whatIsIt: After falling ~19% in May on optimism about a US–Iran 60-day truce framework, oil reversed Monday as Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency reported that Tehran had halted talks with the US in protest of Israel's expanded Lebanon ground operation following the capture of Beaufort Castle. WTI added roughly 6% to ~$92, Brent added ~5% to ~$95.
explainer.howItWorks: Israeli PM Netanyahu ordered an expansion of the Lebanon manoeuvre Sunday after IDF forces seized Beaufort Castle; Lebanese PM Salam called it a 'scorched-earth policy'. Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said US message exchanges continue but 'nothing is certain until a deal is finalised'. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington would resume Iran strikes if the ceasefire talks collapse — the same posture that ran oil to ~$112 in May.

Energy equities (XOM, CVX, SLB, OXY) snap back; refiners and airlines (DAL, UAL, AAL) catch a near-term margin headwind. A re-escalation also threatens the inflation glide-path the Fed is targeting into Warsh's first FOMC.

items.summary: FedEx Freight Holding (NYSE: FDXF) began trading June 1 after FedEx distributed one FDXF share for every two FDX shares held at the May 15 record. S&P Dow Jones is fast-tracking FDXF into the S&P 500 before the June 2 open replacing EPAM; FDXF also joins Dow Transports replacing AAL. FDX -~17% on the ex-distribution price reset.

explainer.tagline: FedEx Freight launches as standalone FDXF and lands a rare same-week S&P 500 fast pass.
explainer.whatIsIt: FedEx completed the tax-free spin-off of its LTL (less-than-truckload) freight unit on June 1, creating FedEx Freight Holding (NYSE: FDXF) as an independent public company under CEO John Smith. FedEx stockholders of record at the May 15 close received one FDXF share for every two FDX shares. FedEx retained a 19.9% stub stake which it must dispose of within 24 months via debt-for-equity exchanges or further distributions.
explainer.howItWorks: S&P Dow Jones gave FDXF the unusual 'fast pass' into the S&P 500 — it joins the index before the June 2 open, replacing EPAM Systems (which drops to the S&P SmallCap 600, where it bumps Shutterstock). FDXF also enters the Dow Jones Transportation Average on June 1, replacing American Airlines. FDX traded down roughly 17% on June 1 — primarily a price re-base reflecting the freight EV leaving the parent, not a fundamental selloff.
explainer.whyItMatters: Forces a mechanical bid for FDXF from S&P 500 index funds before the June 2 open and a mirror sell in EPAM; same dynamic in transports for AAL. The fast-pass into the S&P 500 (without the usual quarterly waiting period) is itself unusual and a positive signal for FDXF's float and liquidity at the open. For FDX itself, the parent now becomes a cleaner Express/Ground story with the cyclical LTL business marked out.

items.title: China May 2026 official PMI — manufacturing slips to 50.0 from 50.3 right at expansion threshold (50.0 est); non-manufacturing 50.1 beats 49.5 consensus as services hold up
items.org: National Bureau of Statistics of China
items.summary: China May NBS manufacturing PMI prints 50.0 (vs 50.0 est, 50.3 prior) — production sub-index 51.2 but new orders 49.9 signal softening demand. Non-manufacturing PMI 50.1 tops 49.5 est.

explainer.tagline: China's official factory gauge falls to the 50.0 expansion-contraction line in May — services hold up at 50.1
explainer.whatIsIt: The National Bureau of Statistics released its May 2026 PMI prints at 09:30 Beijing time on Saturday May 31. The official manufacturing PMI dropped 0.3 points to 50.0, matching the Reuters/Bloomberg consensus of 50.0 and sitting right at the threshold separating expansion from contraction. The official non-manufacturing/services gauge slipped to 50.1, but that beat the 49.5 consensus.
explainer.howItWorks: Inside the manufacturing print, the production sub-index stayed firmly in expansion at 51.2 while new orders dipped to 49.9 — output is holding up but demand is softening. NBS chief statistician Huo Lihui flagged that high-tech manufacturing PMI hit 52.9 (+0.7) for a 16th straight month above 50 and equipment manufacturing held at 52.1 (+0.3); large enterprises rose 0.9 points to 51.1, while smaller firms remained the soft spot. The five-day public-holiday break and Middle-East-driven input-cost pressure both weighed.
explainer.whyItMatters: China is the swing input for the global manufacturing cycle and the prints land before Monday's Asia open — CSI 300, Hang Seng, copper, iron ore and the offshore yuan all trade off the official PMIs. A 50.0 manufacturing print sustains the case for additional Beijing stimulus and pressures the 7.20-7.30 USD/CNY band; the services beat keeps a floor under consumption-linked names. Watch the Caixin manufacturing release next week for the private-sector cross-check.

items.title: S&P 500 logs ninth straight weekly gain — longest streak since 2023 — as Dow closes above 51,000 for first time ever on May 29

explainer.whatIsIt: U.S. equity benchmarks finished Friday May 29 at fresh records to wrap up an eighth straight winning month for the Nasdaq and a ninth straight winning week for the S&P 500. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 363.49 points (+0.72%) to 51,032.46 — the first close above 51,000 in its history. The S&P 500 added 0.22% to 7,580.06, and the Nasdaq Composite ticked up 0.20% to 26,972.62. U.S. markets are closed Monday June 1 only if a holiday applies; June trading resumes Monday June 2.

Friday's headline driver was Dell Technologies, which surged about 33% after its Thursday-night AI-server blowout and raised FY27 revenue guide of $165–$169B with $60B in AI servers. HPE +12% and SMCI traded sympathetically. Costco slipped about 0.85% after Wednesday's Q3 print and a 4.6% intraday drawdown on margin compression. President Trump's late-day Truth Social post that he would make a 'final determination' on an Iran ceasefire after a Situation Room meeting added a geopolitical tailwind into the close.
explainer.whyItMatters: Three-record-high closes on the same day, with a Dow that has now added more than 450 points in nine of the past forty trading sessions, signal that the AI-capex bid is still the dominant marginal flow and that the falling Iran-war risk premium is now priced into long-only books. The breadth question remains live: small caps (Russell 2000 -0.55% Friday) lagged again. Watch this week's ISM Manufacturing print (Monday June 2) and the May payrolls report (Friday June 6) as the next macro tests of the rally.

Investors withdrew roughly $2.8B over the run, including a record single-day outflow from BlackRock's IBIT this week tied to a $1.29B dark-pool block.

explainer.tagline: Nine straight sessions of net selling pulled $2.8B from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs — the longest outflow streak in their 16-month history.
explainer.whatIsIt: U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows in each of the nine trading sessions ending Thursday May 29, totalling roughly $2.8 billion. CoinDesk and Farside Investors flag this as the longest negative streak since the funds began trading in January 2024 — eclipsing the prior six-day record set in late January and the six-day run flagged on May 22.

Weekly outflows ran about $1.3B, with monthly outflows for May totalling roughly $2.3B. Bitcoin's spot price slid from about $80,000 at the start of the streak to about $73,000 by late in the run before recovering modestly. The May 22 spot-ether ETF outflow streak (10 sessions) extended further into the week as well.
explainer.whyItMatters: ETF flows are the cleanest read on incremental U.S. institutional crypto demand. A record streak at this magnitude signals allocators are rotating into the AI-equity rally and away from beta crypto — bitcoin's 2026 YTD return is now about -11%, lagging the Nasdaq's +20%-plus. Counter-read from CoinDesk: prior multi-week outflow runs in February and November coincided with local price bottoms before institutional flows turned positive again.

items.title: Buckle Q1 FY26 — net sales $288.7M (+6.1% Y/Y) and EPS $0.92 beat ($0.74 est) helped by $19.1M interchange settlement; comps +5.1% but BKE -5.84% to $47.70 as gross margin slips 50bp on tariffs
items.summary: Buckle Q1 FY26 — net sales $288.7M (+6.1% Y/Y) beat $287.7M est, diluted EPS $0.92 trounces $0.74 est on a $19.1M interchange-fee litigation settlement boost; comp store sales +5.1% and online +2.8%. Gross margin slipped 50bp to 46.2% on tariffs and occupancy costs; BKE -5.84% to $47.70 on the day.

explainer.tagline: Buckle beats Q1 on a one-time interchange settlement, but tariffs and occupancy chip 50bp from gross margin and the stock falls 5.8% on the print.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Buckle, Inc. — the Nebraska-based denim and casual-apparel chain — reported first quarter fiscal 2026 results before the open on Friday May 29. Net sales for the 13-week quarter ended May 2, 2026 rose 6.1% to $288.7 million from $272.1 million a year earlier. Basic EPS came in at $0.93 and diluted EPS at $0.92, up from $0.70 last year. Comparable store net sales rose 5.1% and online sales grew 2.8% to $47.7 million.
explainer.howItWorks: The headline EPS beat versus the $0.74 consensus was meaningfully helped by a $19.1 million payment from interchange-fee litigation, recorded as a reduction of selling expense — without it, EPS would have been closer to consensus. Gross margin fell 50 basis points to 46.2% from 46.7% as higher occupancy and merchandise costs (including tariff impact) outpaced sales growth. Buckle ended the quarter with 442 stores across 42 states, up from 439 a year ago, and has since opened three more and closed one to reach 444. Strength was concentrated in women's and kids' apparel; menswear lagged.
explainer.whyItMatters: Even with the interchange windfall, the 50bp gross-margin slip frames a clear read for small/mid-cap specialty retail: tariff cost is still leaking through despite the May 13 FCC EchoStar / IEEPA-refund tailwinds, and 2026 store-expansion overhead is being absorbed unevenly. Pair the BKE reaction with Friday's Genesco beat-and-stock-up and Dick's Sporting Goods' tariff-driven 281bp gross-margin hit from earlier in the week — the read across specialty retail this earnings cycle is comp resilience but margin compression.

items.title: AST SpaceMobile -14.79% to $113.41 on May 29 — Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes on Cape Canaveral pad during static-fire test, raising delay fears for the 45-satellite BlueBird rollout; Deutsche Bank downgrades to $106 PT
items.summary: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded during a static-fire test at Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36 on Thursday May 28 around 9pm EDT, scrubbing a June 4 Amazon Leo launch and damaging Blue Origin's only operational New Glenn pad. ASTS -14.79% to $113.41 on 47.8M shares (159% above 3-mo avg) as Deutsche Bank cuts PT to $106; RKLB -6%, PL -8%, LUNR -5%.

metrics.Blue Origin pad status: Only operational New Glenn pad damaged
metrics.Scrubbed mission: First of 24 Amazon Leo launches (NET June 4)

explainer.tagline: Blue Origin's only New Glenn pad blows up on a static-fire — and the space-stock rally that was riding SpaceX-IPO euphoria takes a punch.
explainer.whatIsIt: Blue Origin's New Glenn heavy-lift rocket exploded on Cape Canaveral's Launch Complex 36 around 9 p.m. EDT on Thursday May 28, 2026 during a routine static-fire ignition test of its seven methane-fueled BE-4 first-stage engines. The rocket was being prepped for a planned NET-June 4 launch carrying the first batch of 24 contracted Amazon Project Kuiper Leo satellites; the payload had not yet been delivered to the pad. All personnel were accounted for and safe, but the launchpad and at least one lightning protection tower were destroyed.
explainer.howItWorks: Jeff Bezos posted on X that 'all personnel are accounted for' and that root-cause work was underway; he added the company will 'rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying.' Blue Origin only has one operational New Glenn pad, the one damaged Thursday night — that's the key supply-side constraint for the launch market. The previous New Glenn flight (NG-3) suffered an upper-stage cryogenic-leak anomaly that already cost AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird-7 satellite the intended orbit, so this is the second high-profile New Glenn miss for AST's network rollout.
explainer.whyItMatters: AST SpaceMobile closed Friday May 29 at $113.41, down 14.79% on 47.8 million shares (about 159% above its three-month average) — its largest single-day drop since the BlueBird launch program began. Deutsche Bank cut its price target to $106 a share, flagging additional schedule risk to the 45-satellite BlueBird constellation that AST has booked across Blue Origin and SpaceX. Sympathy moves hit RKLB -6%+, Planet Labs -8%, and Intuitive Machines -5%; the Procure Space ETF (UFO) had its worst session of the year. The sector had been rallying ahead of SpaceX's S-1 filing — Friday's selloff repriced launch-cadence risk back into the names that depend on third-party rides.
explainer.forWho: space-economy traders, single-stock space longs, ETF arb desks

items.title: Reportedly: U.S. and Iran reach tentative 60-day truce extension and Strait of Hormuz reopening framework on May 29 — Trump 'final determination' pending from Situation Room; Brent -1.4% to $91.37, WTI -2% to ~$87 (6-week low)
items.summary: Tentative U.S.-Iran MoU extends ceasefire 60 days and restores unrestricted Strait of Hormuz shipping; Trump heads to Situation Room for 'final determination' Friday; Brent settles -1.4% at $91.37, WTI -2% near 6-week low.

explainer.tagline: Negotiators land a 60-day ceasefire extension + Hormuz-reopening MoU; markets price an oil-supply unfreeze before Trump signs.
explainer.whatIsIt: Bloomberg, Al Jazeera and others reported May 29 that U.S. and Iranian negotiators reached a memorandum of understanding to extend the current ceasefire by 60 days and restore unrestricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively shut since February 28. President Trump posted Friday that he was heading to the Situation Room for a 'final determination,' but Iranian state media said the text is not yet finalized.
explainer.howItWorks: The MoU framework: (1) ceasefire extended 60 days from Friday; (2) follow-on nuclear talks during the 60-day window; (3) Hormuz reopening with 'no tolls' for unrestricted shipping traffic. Trump's stated conditions are that Iran 'never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb' and the Strait reopens 'immediately.' No signed text as of Friday close.
explainer.whyItMatters: Oil priced the headline aggressively: Brent settled $91.37 (-1.43%) and WTI fell about 2% to ~$87.20 — the lowest in roughly six weeks and on track for a ~17% May decline. About a fifth of global oil and LNG flows transit Hormuz, so confirmation would compress the supply premium further. A Trump rejection or Iranian walk-back snaps the move; this is a setup-driven trade, not a fact-yet.
explainer.forWho: Energy desks, EM/petro-FX, defense names, geopolitical risk overlays.

items.title: Surface Transportation Board pauses Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern $85B merger review — accepts revised application but demands supplemental data by July 27; UNP -4.2%, NSC -4.9%
items.summary: STB unanimously accepted the UP–NS revised merger application (Docket FD 36873) but held proceedings — including environmental review — in abeyance, ordering supplemental info by July 27, 2026. UP and NSC slip ~4–5% as the combined-close target slides from April 2027 to mid-2027.

explainer.tagline: Regulator hits pause on what would be America's first true transcontinental Class I rail merger.
explainer.whatIsIt: Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) agreed earlier this year to buy Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC) in an all-stock deal valued around $85B — combining the largest western and a major eastern Class I railroad into the first single-line transcontinental network. Class I rail mergers require Surface Transportation Board approval under 49 CFR Part 1180.
explainer.howItWorks: The STB unanimously accepted the parties' revised merger application (filed April 30, 2026) for consideration but found portions 'unclear or underdeveloped'. The Board paused the formal evidentiary schedule and environmental review and ordered supplemental information by July 27, 2026, covering competition impact, 2-to-1/3-to-2 shipper access, diversion analysis, gateway treatment, service assurance, downstream M&A effects and passenger-rail coexistence. UP and NSC fell about 4–5% on the day as the timeline slipped.
explainer.whyItMatters: The pause adds an estimated ~60 days to the regulatory clock and pushes the targeted close from April 2027 to mid-2027. Deal-arb spreads on UNP and NSC widened on the print. Approval odds remain intact per most sell-side commentary, but the longer process raises the risk that conditions get attached, which would compress synergy upside on the largest US rail M&A ever.
explainer.forWho: M&A arb desks, industrials/transports analysts, rail-focused PMs

explainer.whatIsIt: Dell Technologies reported first quarter fiscal 2027 results after the close on Thursday May 28. Q1 revenue jumped 88% year-over-year to a record $43.8 billion. Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.86 was up 214%, and GAAP EPS of $5.24 was up 282%. Both metrics blew past Street consensus.
explainer.howItWorks: Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue hit a record $29.0 billion, up 181% Y/Y, with AI-Optimized Servers revenue of $16.1 billion up 757%. Dell booked $24.4 billion of AI orders in the quarter and lifted its FY27 AI server revenue outlook to roughly $60 billion (up 144% Y/Y), from the prior $50B target. Full-year FY27 revenue guide is now $165–$169 billion (midpoint $167B, +47% Y/Y) — up from $138–$142B prior. Operating cash flow was a Q1-record $4.1B; the company returned $2.1B to shareholders ($1.628B buybacks + $464M dividends).
explainer.whyItMatters: Dell is the largest deployer of Blackwell-class systems outside the hyperscalers, so the $24.4B AI orders print and the $60B FY27 server target are direct read-throughs for NVIDIA, Broadcom and the AI-power complex. The 47% raise to full-year revenue guidance, after a +158% YTD share-price run into the print, removes the most-watched 'is the AI capex cycle peaking' bear case. HPE and SMCI now have a steep bar to clear into their own prints.

items.title: U.S. April 2026 PCE — headline +3.8% Y/Y (highest since May 2023) and core +3.3% Y/Y (highest since Oct 2023), but M/M comes in cooler than feared at +0.4% headline / +0.2% core
items.summary: April PCE rose 0.4% M/M (vs +0.5% est) and 3.8% Y/Y. Core PCE rose 0.2% M/M (vs +0.3% est) and 3.3% Y/Y. Personal income was flat and the savings rate slipped to 2.6% as Iran-driven energy costs squeeze the consumer.

explainer.tagline: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge hits a three-year high on the year-over-year measure, but cooler month-over-month components blunt the worst-case stagflation read.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Bureau of Economic Analysis released the April 2026 Personal Income and Outlays report on Thursday May 28 at 8:30am ET. Headline PCE rose 0.4% on the month — below the 0.5% consensus and a step down from March's 0.7% — and 3.8% over the prior twelve months, matching expectations and the highest annual reading since May 2023. Core PCE rose 0.2% M/M (vs +0.3% est) and 3.3% Y/Y, the hottest annual core reading since October 2023.
explainer.howItWorks: Personal income was essentially flat (-$0.1B) and the personal saving rate dipped to 2.6% of disposable income as nominal PCE outran take-home pay. Spending mix was services-led ($67.2B) with goods adding $44.0B. The Y/Y acceleration vs March (3.5% headline, 3.2% core) lines up with the April CPI passthrough from the Iran/Israel oil shock, but the cooler M/M signals the worst monthly impulse may have peaked.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the second hot inflation print of the post-Powell era under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and lands the same morning as the Q1 GDP downward revision to +1.6% — a textbook stagflation tape. Fed-funds futures already priced essentially zero 2026 cuts; a Y/Y at multi-year highs keeps that pricing intact, but the cooler M/M may cap the rates selloff. 10Y, 30Y and DXY all reactive on the release.
explainer.forWho: macro and rates desks tracking the Fed-transition and stagflation trade

items.title: U.S. Q1 2026 GDP revised down to +1.6% from +2.0% advance — corporate profits growth slows to $40.4B vs $246.9B in Q4 2025
items.summary: Real Q1 GDP revised down 0.4pp to a +1.6% annualized pace on softer investment and consumer spending. Real GDI rose just 0.9% and corporate profits added only $40.4B vs $246.9B in Q4 2025 — a sharp slowdown.

explainer.tagline: BEA's Q1 second estimate cuts growth to 1.6% — corporate profits flatline as the soft-landing narrative softens further alongside hot PCE.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Bureau of Economic Analysis released the Q1 2026 GDP second estimate on Thursday May 28 at 8:30am ET. Real GDP grew at a 1.6% annualized pace in Q1, revised down 0.4 percentage points from the April 30 advance estimate of 2.0%. The downward revision was primarily driven by lower-than-previously-estimated investment and consumer spending.
explainer.howItWorks: Real gross domestic income (GDI) rose only 0.9% in Q1 (vs +1.6% in Q4 2025); the average of real GDP and real GDI — the BEA's preferred two-side check — landed at +1.3%. Corporate profits before tax rose just $40.4B in Q1, a stark deceleration from the $246.9B gain in Q4 2025. Net exports stayed positive and government spending continued to add to growth.
explainer.whyItMatters: This print drops alongside the hot April PCE — headline 3.8% Y/Y, core 3.3% Y/Y — sharpening the stagflation tape. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow tracker and Q2 nowcasts now matter more for the soft-landing call. Equity desks watch profits growth as the next test for index-level earnings revisions; rates desks watch GDI weakness vs sticky PCE for cut-path discounting.
explainer.forWho: macro desks, asset allocators, fixed-income strategists

explainer.tagline: Pentagon hands Dell Federal Systems a five-year $9.7B vehicle to centralize Microsoft software buying across the U.S. military.
explainer.whatIsIt: On Wednesday May 27, the Department of Defense awarded Dell Federal Systems a five-year contract worth ~$9.7B, known as the Microsoft Department of War Enterprise Software Agreement II Core Enterprise Technology Agreement. The award was announced at a Pentagon briefing by DoD Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies and acting Navy CIO Barry Tanner after a competitive process.
explainer.howItWorks: Under the deal Dell will provide Microsoft 365, advanced cloud subscriptions and on-premises licensing capability across the Department of Defense, the intelligence community and the U.S. Coast Guard. Davies told reporters the consolidation is expected to save the department about $422M per year by replacing fragmented buying habits with a single procurement vehicle. Microsoft is the underlying software vendor; Dell is the prime contractor and integrator.
explainer.whyItMatters: Dell's federal franchise was already a hidden ballast inside the AI-server narrative; the contract adds a multi-year recurring services tail at meaningful scale and reinforces Dell's position as the Pentagon's preferred IT systems integrator. Microsoft retains the underlying software revenue. Dell reports Q1 FY27 earnings tonight after the close, so the print will frame how analysts model federal recurring revenue going forward.

explainer.tagline: Fresh U.S. strikes on Iran around the Strait of Hormuz and an IRGC missile at a U.S. base in Kuwait test the May 23 ceasefire, dragging oil higher on Hormuz-reopening risk.
explainer.whatIsIt: U.S. Central Command carried out fresh military action against Iran late on May 27 and into May 28. American forces intercepted four Iranian one-way attack drones threatening U.S. assets near the Strait of Hormuz and then struck a ground-control station on the outskirts of Bandar Abbas airport before it could launch a fifth drone. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait at 4:50 a.m. local time in response, and warned that any further U.S. strikes would bring a 'more decisive' Iranian response.
explainer.howItWorks: U.S. officials described the Bandar Abbas strike as 'measured, purely defensive and intended to maintain the ceasefire' agreed during Trump's May 23 framework announcement. Iran's foreign ministry condemned the action as a 'blatant violation' of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. Kuwait's air defenses were activated against the IRGC missile-and-drone threat. Three explosions were reported east of Bandar Abbas, a strategic port and naval base on the Iranian side of the Strait of Hormuz.
explainer.whyItMatters: Brent rose to $96.19 (+2.02%) and WTI to $90.41 (+1.95%) on Thursday, erasing much of Wednesday's decline that had been driven by hopes the Strait of Hormuz would reopen under the May 23 framework. The renewed flare-up keeps the energy-driven inflation channel — visible in this morning's PCE print — live. items.summary: Salesforce's record Q1 trounces on EPS and showcases $1.2B Agentforce ARR (+205%), but a Q2 revenue guide below consensus pressures CRM ~3% AH as AI-anxiety questions linger.

explainer.tagline: Salesforce beats Q1 and triples AI+Data ARR to $3.4B but the Q2 revenue guide undershoots — CRM slips ~3% AH.
explainer.whatIsIt: Salesforce reported Q1 fiscal 2027 results on May 27, 2026 after the close. The print showed record quarterly revenue, EPS well above consensus, and a sharp acceleration in the Agentforce + Data 360 franchise — but Q2 revenue guidance came in slightly under Street expectations and the stock pulled back in extended hours.
explainer.howItWorks: Revenue was $11.13B (+13% Y/Y, +12% CC) and non-GAAP EPS $3.88 (+50%) crushed a ~$3.12 estimate; GAAP EPS hit $2.42 (+52%). Current RPO grew 14% to $33.6B. Agentforce ARR reached $1.2B, up 205% Y/Y, with combined AI + Data 360 ARR at $3.4B (+200%). FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $45.9–$46.2B (11% growth) with non-GAAP operating margin of 34.3%, while Q2 was guided to $11.27–$11.35B versus a ~$11.36B Street view.
explainer.whyItMatters: Salesforce came in down 32% YTD entering the print, with bears arguing AI agents would cannibalise the seat-based SaaS model. Agentforce ARR more than tripling proves the agentic upsell is materialising, but the Q2 guide reinforces the slower headline-growth narrative that has dogged the name and keeps the AI-disruption-vs-monetisation debate alive across CRM, NOW, and ADBE.

items.title: Dick's Sporting Goods Q1 FY26 — first combined quarter with Foot Locker delivers $5.16B sales (+62.7% Y/Y), DICK'S comp +6.0% and FL proforma comp +0.6% returning to growth and profit; FY26 non-GAAP EPS guide $13.50–$14.50 maintained and segment comps raised; DKS ~-2% premarket as 281bp gross-margin hit lands
items.summary: DICK'S first quarter as combined retailer: $5.16B in sales, Foot Locker $1.79B contribution returns to comp growth and profit; raised segment comp ranges but 281bp gross-margin hit drags DKS ~-2% premarket.

explainer.tagline: First combined quarter: DICK'S +6% comp, Foot Locker back to growth and profit, but a 281bp gross-margin hit lands.
explainer.whatIsIt: DICK'S Sporting Goods reported Q1 FY26 results before the open on May 27, 2026 — the company's first quarter operating with Foot Locker after the early-2026 close. The print showcased the integration paying off on top-line and Foot Locker turnaround, but acquisition-related inventory write-downs hit the gross-margin line and the FY26 GAAP EPS guide moved lower.
explainer.howItWorks: Consolidated net sales jumped 62.7% to $5.165B as the Foot Locker business contributed $1.787B in its first full quarter, with a proforma comp of +0.6% — its first positive comp print under the new owner. The DICK'S business comped +6.0% and produced $361.0M in segment profit; Foot Locker booked $17.5M of segment profit. Consolidated gross margin compressed 281bp to 32.59% on a $42.7M Foot Locker inventory write-down. Management raised the low end of both segment comp ranges (DICK'S now +2.5%–+4.0%, Foot Locker +1.5%–+3.0%), held non-GAAP EPS guidance at $13.50–$14.50, and lowered GAAP EPS guidance to $13.27–$14.27.
explainer.whyItMatters: This is the first proof-point that the Foot Locker buyback (the 'Fast Break' plan) can deliver same-store-sales growth and profitability quickly — important for athletic-channel peers including Nike, Adidas wholesale, On, and Foot Locker comp tickers' read-through. The premarket dip ties the print to broader retail sensitivity on gross-margin and inventory write-down cadence.
explainer.forWho: Retail and athletic-sector analysts

items.title: Verra Mobility crashes ~41% AH on May 26 — Avis Budget Group terminates Commercial Services agreement effective Sept 2026; cuts 2026 revenue guide by $135–$145M and adj EBITDA guide by ~$120M
items.summary: Avis Budget — Verra Mobility's largest Commercial Services customer at >10% of total revenue — terminates the agreement; VRRM cuts FY26 revenue guide to $985–$995M and slumps -41% AH to $7.70.

explainer.tagline: Verra Mobility loses its single largest customer — Avis Budget terminates the tolling/violation-services contract that powered >10% of total revenue.
explainer.whatIsIt: Verra Mobility (the company behind in-vehicle tolling and rental-car violation processing) disclosed on May 26 that Avis Budget Group has issued a contract-termination notice. The termination is effective September 2026. Avis represented more than 10% of Verra's total revenue in Q1 2026 and FY2025.
explainer.howItWorks: Verra now expects FY26 total revenue of $985M–$995M, adj EBITDA of $380M–$385M, adj EPS of $1.19–$1.25, and free cash flow of $140M–$150M. The Commercial Services segment loses an estimated $135M–$145M of annualized revenue and $120M–$125M of annualized segment profit, before any cost offsets. CEO David Roberts said the company was 'surprised and disappointed' given the longstanding partnership.
explainer.whyItMatters: Customer concentration risk was a long-running bear case; the print confirms it. VRRM dropped -41.2% to $7.70 in after-hours trading on May 26 — a multi-year low — wiping ~$700M of market cap. The company says it will pursue contractual and IP remedies and re-deploy resources to other rental and fleet customers, but the segment-level damage is structural.
explainer.forWho: small/mid-cap fund managers, mobility-fintech analysts

items.title: Abercrombie & Fitch Q1 FY26 — record $1.1B net sales (+2%) and EPS $1.47 above outlook on Americas +3% / APAC +24% strength; EMEA -10% as Mideast war bites Hollister; $105M Q1 buyback and FY26 outlook reaffirmed; ANF +~6% premarket
items.summary: ANF's 14th straight quarter of growth — record Q1 sales $1.1B and operating margin 8.0%. EPS $1.47 beats analyst ~$1.27 est; FY26 EPS guide of $10.20–$11.00 reaffirmed; $105M repurchased; +6.2% premarket to $78.99.

explainer.tagline: ANF prints its 14th straight growth quarter — beat on EPS, miss on top line, but Americas + APAC offset Mideast-driven EMEA weakness.
explainer.whatIsIt: Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q1 FY26 (quarter ended May 2, 2026) before the open on May 27. Net sales were a record $1.1B, up 2% Y/Y, with the company logging its 14th consecutive quarter of growth. Diluted EPS came in at $1.47, ahead of the company's own outlook and well above sell-side estimates near $1.27.
explainer.howItWorks: Brand mix: Abercrombie brands +3%, Hollister brands flat. Regional mix: Americas +3%, APAC +24%, EMEA -10% as the ongoing Middle East war softened demand, particularly for Hollister. Operating margin landed at 8.0%. The company repurchased $105M of stock in Q1 (~3% of shares outstanding at the start of the year).
explainer.whyItMatters: ANF reaffirmed FY26 sales growth guide of 3–5%, EPS guide of $10.20–$11.00, and ~$450M of full-year buybacks; Q2 guide is sales +2–4% and EPS $1.80–$2.00 with at least $150M more in repurchases. The print pushed ANF +6.2% premarket to $78.99 — a vote of confidence that the brand engine still has legs despite EMEA war headwinds.

items.title: Bath & Body Works Q1 FY26 — net sales $1.38B (-3% Y/Y) beat $1.36B est, adj EPS $0.32 and GAAP EPS $0.90 trounce estimates; reaffirms FY26 guide and announces CFO Eva Boratto departing June 12; BBWI +17% premarket to $20.78
items.summary: BBWI's Q1 results 'exceeded guidance' despite the soft top line. Adj operating income $151M, adj EPS $0.32, GAAP EPS $0.90. FY26 sales/EPS guidance reaffirmed. CFO Eva Boratto departs June 12; stock soars +17.2% premarket.

explainer.tagline: BBWI's Q1 lands above its own guidance — beat on every line, but CFO is leaving and the brand admits it's 'below the standard.'
explainer.whatIsIt: Bath & Body Works reported Q1 FY26 (quarter ended May 2, 2026) before the open on May 27. Net sales fell 3.2% Y/Y to $1.38B (a slight beat vs $1.36B est). GAAP diluted EPS was $0.90, adjusted EPS $0.32. Adjusted operating income $151M, adjusted net income $65M.
explainer.howItWorks: CEO Daniel Heaf characterized the results as 'exceeded guidance, but remain below the standard our brand is capable of delivering' and pointed to the Consumer First Formula reset. The company reaffirmed its FY26 outlook: net sales down 4.5%–2.5% versus FY25's $7.29B; GAAP EPS $3.00–$3.25; adjusted EPS $2.40–$2.65. CFO Eva Boratto will step down effective June 12; Tom Javitch named interim CFO while an active search runs.
explainer.whyItMatters: After a sluggish full year, an above-guide beat was the read the market needed — BBWI +17.2% premarket to $20.78. The CFO transition is the wrinkle: combining a leadership change with an admitted 'below standard' brand assessment leaves a long runway for proof points, but Q1 buys management some room.
explainer.forWho: consumer-discretionary investors, specialty-retail analysts

items.summary: PDD reports Q1 2026: revenue RMB106.2B (+11%) and operating profit RMB19.6B (+22%) beat the top, but net income fell 15% and non-GAAP EPS/ADS RMB9.51 (~$1.38) missed; ADS slumps ~8% premarket on margin compression.

explainer.tagline: PDD's Q1 2026 cracks the same way Q4 did — revenue holds up but profit shrinks as China e-commerce subsidies and Temu's tariff fight bite.
explainer.whatIsIt: PDD Holdings (parent of Pinduoduo and Temu) reported Q1 2026 before the U.S. open on May 27. Total revenue grew 11% Y/Y to RMB106.2B ($15.4B), with transaction services revenue up 20% to RMB56.3B and online marketing revenue roughly flat at RMB49.9B.
explainer.howItWorks: Operating profit rose 22% to RMB19.6B and non-GAAP operating profit rose 15% to RMB21.1B — but lower-line metrics weakened. Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders fell 15% Y/Y to RMB12.5B and non-GAAP net income dropped 17% to RMB14.1B. Investors took it as confirmation that the China-domestic merchant subsidy program and Temu's U.S. tariff exposure are still eating into PDD's structural margin. ADS dropped ~8.4% to $88.51 in premarket trading, lopping roughly $13B off market cap.

items.title: Micron crosses $1T market cap for first time as UBS lifts PT to Street-high $1,625 — MU +~19% on May 26, +213% YTD; UBS sees HBM4 sold out and EPS staying above $100 through 2029
items.summary: Micron jumps ~19% to ~$895.88 and tops $1T market cap for the first time on May 26 after UBS's Timothy Arcuri lifts PT to a Street-high $1,625 (from $535) on sold-out HBM4 and AI-memory long-term agreements.

explainer.tagline: Micron joins the trillion-dollar club as UBS triples its price target on sold-out HBM4 and structural AI-memory pricing.
explainer.whatIsIt: Micron Technology shares jumped about 19% on Tuesday May 26, closing near $895.88 and pushing the memory-chip maker's market value above $1 trillion for the first time. The catalyst was a UBS note from analyst Timothy Arcuri lifting his price target to a new Street-high $1,625 from $535 — a 204% revision.
explainer.howItWorks: Arcuri argued Micron's 2026 HBM4 capacity is already sold out under long-term, fixed-price agreements, with DRAM contract prices up 58–63% and NAND up 70–75% year-to-date. UBS modeled cumulative free cash flow above $400B from 2027–2029 and EPS above $100 even in a 'moderate memory downcycle' through 2029. Other memory names rallied in sympathy — SanDisk +~7%, Western Digital +~8%, Seagate +~4%.
explainer.whyItMatters: Micron is now the 11th-largest US public company by market cap, ahead of Walmart, marking memory's reclassification from a commodity cycle play to AI infrastructure. The Nasdaq closed at a fresh record 26,656.18 (+1.19%) led by the semis bid, and Polymarket priced ~34% odds of a US government equity stake in Micron by year-end. The structural-LTA framing — fixed volume + partially fixed price — is the bull thesis for the entire memory complex.
explainer.forWho: semis traders, AI-infra investors

items.title: Zscaler Q3 FY26 — revenue $850.5M (+25% Y/Y) and ARR $3.525B (+25%) top, raises FY26 EPS to $4.10–$4.11, but cuts FY26 FCF margin guide to 22.8–23.3% from 26.5–27% on higher capex; ZS -~17 to -20% AH
items.summary: Zscaler beat on Q3 with $850.5M revenue (+25% Y/Y), $3.525B ARR and $1.08 non-GAAP EPS, and raised the FY26 EPS guide; but the FCF margin guide was cut to 22.8–23.3% on higher AI/data-center capex, sending ZS ~17–20% lower after hours.

explainer.tagline: Zscaler beat on Q3 and raised FY guides — then sliced its free-cash-flow margin outlook on AI capex, and the stock fell ~17–20% AH.
explainer.whatIsIt: Zscaler reported fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended April 30) revenue of $850.5M (+25% Y/Y), ARR of $3.525B (+25%), non-GAAP EPS of $1.08 (vs $1.04 est), and a record 23% non-GAAP operating margin. Management raised the FY26 ARR, revenue, op income, and EPS guides — but cut the full-year free cash flow margin guide to 22.8–23.3% from 26.5–27% to fund higher data-center capex.
explainer.howItWorks: Q3 net new ARR was $166M (+24% Y/Y); excluding the Red Canary acquisition (which added $127M of ARR), organic ARR growth was 21% and net new ARR grew 14%. The new FY26 EPS guide of $4.10–$4.11 implies +25% growth. Capex is now expected in the high single-digits as a percentage of revenue, primarily for AI inference capacity tied to new Project Glasswing, OpenAI Day-Break and Project AI-Guardian initiatives.
explainer.whyItMatters: Zscaler's reaction is the latest SaaS-pays-the-AI-capex story — investors penalized the FCF guide cut despite raised top-line and EPS guides, knocking ~$7B off market cap after hours. Watch read-through to other security and infra-SaaS names that face the same capex/margin tradeoff (CRWD, NET, OKTA, S, PANW).

items.summary: Box Q1 FY27 (quarter ended April 30) revenue of $306M was up 11% Y/Y — its first double-digit growth in over three years — with non-GAAP EPS $0.37 beating $0.36 guidance, but the FY27 revenue guide of ~$1.275B and EPS guide of ~$1.56 vs $1.63 consensus sent BOX ~4% lower AH.

items.title: Insulet initiates voluntary Medical Device Correction on Omnipod 5 / DASH / Eros pods — ~7M pods in scope on cannula-tear risk; expects up to $50M 2026 cost (excluded from adj results); PODD -~6% AH
items.summary: Insulet announces a voluntary MDC for specific lots of Omnipod 5, DASH, and Eros pods after identifying a manufacturing issue that can cause cannula tears and insulin under-delivery; ~7M pods in scope (~60% already used/expired), up to $50M 2026 cost; PODD slides ~6% after hours.

explainer.tagline: Insulet flags a second cannula-tear correction in two months — ~7M Omnipod pods in scope with up to $50M in 2026 cleanup costs.
explainer.whatIsIt: Insulet initiated a voluntary Medical Device Correction on specific lots of Omnipod 5, Omnipod DASH, and Omnipod Eros pods on May 26, after identifying a manufacturing issue that can produce a small tear in the cannula just above the skin — potentially leading to insulin leaking outside the pod rather than being delivered to the patient.
explainer.howItWorks: Approximately 7M pods are in scope (about 8.5% of 2025 global Omnipod production), with ~60% already consumed or expired. Globally, 24 serious adverse events have been reported including hospitalizations and diabetic ketoacidosis, but no deaths. The action is separate from Insulet's March 12, 2026 voluntary correction; both stem from cannula handling at the Acton, MA facility but involve different manufacturing processes. Insulet expects up to $50M of 2026 costs, which will be excluded from adjusted results.
explainer.whyItMatters: Insulet kept its previously issued FY26 financial and long-term growth guide unchanged, but PODD slid ~6% after hours — investors are now stacking two cannula-related corrections from the same facility in two months, raising questions about quality systems. Read-through to diabetes-tech peers TNDM, MDT, DXCM on share-shift risk if patients switch pumps.
explainer.forWho: medtech investors, diabetes-tech sector

items.title: AutoZone Q3 FY26 — net sales $4.84B (+8.4% Y/Y), EPS $38.07 beats ~$36.13 est; total SSS +3.9% (domestic +4.1%); $586M Q3 buyback as store count crosses 7,856
items.summary: AutoZone Q3 FY26: $4.84B revenue (+8.4%), EPS $38.07 trounces $36.13 est on $923.8M operating profit (+6.6%). Total comps +3.9%, domestic +4.1%, international +1.6%. $586.3M repurchased; $0.8B left on authorization.

explainer.tagline: AutoZone's third quarter beats on EPS and clears the 3% comp bar despite a revenue nick — buyback machine keeps chugging.
explainer.whatIsIt: Auto-parts retailer AutoZone reported fiscal third-quarter results before the bell on May 26, 2026 for the 12 weeks ended May 9. The print is the first read on US DIY auto demand into the Memorial Day setup and a marker for whether tariff-driven cost pressure is showing up in margins.
explainer.howItWorks: Net sales rose 8.4% Y/Y to $4.84B (versus ~$4.86B consensus), while diluted EPS climbed to $38.07 from $35.36 — beating the ~$36.13 Street estimate. Total same-store sales rose 3.9% on a constant-currency basis (domestic +4.1%, international +1.6%). Operating profit was $923.8M (+6.6%), but gross margin slipped 57bp on a 77bp non-cash LIFO drag. Net income reached $641.5M (vs $608.4M). Buybacks totalled $586.3M (164K shares at ~$3,582 average), with $0.8B remaining on the authorization. Store count ended at 7,856 (US 6,766; Mexico 933; Brazil 157).
explainer.whyItMatters: AZO's comp acceleration to +4.1% domestic — back above the 3% level that signals real DIY traffic — supports the bull thesis on US auto-aftermarket demand and contrasts with mixed retail prints from WMT and TGT last week. The LIFO-driven gross margin slip is the soft spot worth watching: a sustained move lower would signal tariff/COGS pressure that mega-cap retailers have been flagging. Peer ORLY and AAP trade on the same comp framework.
explainer.forWho: Consumer discretionary investors and retail desks gauging DIY auto demand.

items.title: KOSPI closes above 8,000 for first time ever — +2.55% to record 8,047.51 on Iran-deal hopes and oil -7%; Samsung +2.22%, SK hynix +5.72% breaks ₩2M/share; foreign net buying ends 13-day selling streak
items.summary: KOSPI rockets +199.80 points (+2.55%) to first-ever close above 8,000 at 8,047.51 — intraday topped 8,131.15. Samsung +2.22%, SK hynix +5.72% past ₩2M for first time, Hyundai Motor +5.19%. Foreigners net buyers after 13 sessions.

explainer.tagline: Seoul's benchmark prints its first-ever 8,000 close as AI memory rallies and Iran-deal optimism crushes oil 7%.
explainer.whatIsIt: South Korea's KOSPI closed above the 8,000 level for the first time in its 43-year history on Tuesday, the same session that the US returned from Memorial Day weekend with futures pointing higher on the same Iran-deal narrative. Korea's index has been on a multi-month chip-led tear; today's break is the next round number after the May 11 close above 7,800.
explainer.howItWorks: KOSPI jumped 199.80 points to settle at 8,047.51 (+2.55%) after spiking as high as 8,131.15 intraday. Samsung Electronics rose 2.22% to ₩301,000 and SK hynix surged 5.72% to ₩2,074,000 — its first close above the ₩2 million mark. Hyundai Motor added 5.19%. Foreign investors flipped to net buyers for the first time in 13 trading sessions. The macro tailwind was oil: Brent July futures fell 7.15% to $96.14 and WTI July fell 6.51% to $90.31 as the US and Iran moved closer to a ceasefire MoU that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
explainer.whyItMatters: Korea is the cleanest single-country read on the AI-memory cycle — HBM (SK hynix) and DRAM (Samsung) pricing translates almost directly into the KOSPI. A first-ever close above 8,000 with oil collapsing on Hormuz-reopen hopes confirms that the macro market sees the Iran de-escalation as durable enough to mark up risk assets. Watch US semis (NVDA, AVGO, MU) at open and the DRAM ETF, which tracks the same memory complex.
explainer.forWho: Asia EM allocators and US semi/AI-infrastructure traders.

items.title: Nikkei 225 tops 65,000 for first time ever — closes +2.87% at 65,158.19 on Sunday Trump 'constructive' Iran post; oil tumbles ~5% on Hormuz-reopening hopes
items.summary: Nikkei 225 punches through 65,000 for the first time in history, closing +2.87% at 65,158.19 as Trump's Sunday Truth Social post calls US-Iran talks 'orderly and constructive'; WTI -~5.8% to ~$91, Taiwan TAIEX +2.91% to record.

explainer.tagline: Japan's Nikkei smashes through 65,000 in holiday-thinned Asia trading as Trump's Sunday Iran note crushes oil and stokes risk-on.
explainer.whatIsIt: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed above 65,000 for the first time in its history on Monday, May 25, jumping 2.87% to 65,158.19 with an intraday peak near 65,254. US markets were closed for Memorial Day and the UK FTSE was shut for the Spring Bank Holiday, leaving Asia and Continental Europe to drive the global tape.
explainer.howItWorks: President Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday May 24 that US-Iran negotiations were 'proceeding in an orderly and constructive manner' and that he had told his representatives 'not to rush into a deal in that time is on our side.' Oil cratered: WTI -5.77% to ~$91.00, Brent below $100 (-~5%). Semis led the Tokyo bid — Kioxia Holdings +5.94% to ¥60,810 on AI-memory demand. Asian peers followed: Taiwan's TAIEX +2.91% to a record 43,495.92, Australia's ASX 200 +0.45%. Europe opened higher, with the DAX +1.6%, CAC 40 +1.8%, and Stoxx 600 at the highest level since March 2.
explainer.whyItMatters: First-ever close above 65,000 caps an ~5% surge for the Nikkei in just three weeks after clearing 62,000 on May 7 — the index is now ~24% above its February 28 pre-war low. The trigger pairing — Trump's softer Iran tone plus falling oil — directly reverses the inflation-from-energy bid that has dragged US 30Y yields above 5% for most of May. JPMorgan now projects Nikkei 70,000 by year-end. UK and US desks return Tuesday to risk-on Asia/Europe and a fresh 'peace dividend' bid in oil.
explainer.forWho: Asia-Pacific equity, global macro, energy traders

items.title: S&P 500 caps eighth straight weekly gain at record 7,473.47 on May 22 — longest streak since 2023; Dow closes at record 50,579.70 on Iran-deal progress
items.summary: S&P 500 +0.37% to record 7,473.47, Dow +0.58% to record 50,579.70, Nasdaq +0.19% to 26,343.97. Eighth straight weekly gain is the longest since 2023, as Iran-deal optimism overrides record-low UMich consumer sentiment heading into the Memorial Day shortened week.

explainer.tagline: S&P 500 logs its eighth straight weekly gain — the longest streak since 2023 — and Dow notches a record close as Iran-deal progress overrides a record-low consumer sentiment print.
explainer.whatIsIt: U.S. equity benchmarks finished Friday May 22 at fresh records to wrap up an eighth straight winning week. The S&P 500 added 0.37% to close at 7,473.47, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 294 points (+0.58%) to a record 50,579.70, and the Nasdaq Composite ticked up 0.19% to 26,343.97. U.S. markets are closed Monday May 25 for Memorial Day.
explainer.howItWorks: The eight-week winning streak is the S&P 500's longest since 2023. Friday's drivers were President Trump's Truth Social post that a U.S.–Iran deal — including a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — is 'largely negotiated', plus the swearing-in of Kevin Warsh as Fed Chair at the White House. Offsetting headwinds: the University of Michigan final May sentiment crashed to 44.8, the lowest reading on record, as gas prices remain near $5/gal.
explainer.whyItMatters: Eight-week winning streaks are rare and historically followed by single-digit pullbacks — the last such streak ended in August 2023. The current rally is being driven by the AI capex complex (Nvidia, Lenovo, Dell, Quanta) and falling Iran-war risk premium, with breadth narrowing as consumer sentiment hits an all-time low. Watch this week's PCE print and Nvidia post-earnings setup as the next macro tests.
explainer.forWho: macro traders, index investors, allocators tracking risk regimes

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed $1.26B in six-day streak through May 22 — worst week since late January; spot Ether ETFs extend 10-day outflow run
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $1.26B across six straight sessions May 15-22 — the worst weekly outflow since late January. Spot ether ETFs lost a further $6.6M on Friday for a tenth consecutive losing session, the longest negative streak since March 2025.

explainer.tagline: Six straight days of net selling pulled $1.26B from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, while ether ETFs extended their losing streak to 10 sessions.
explainer.whatIsIt: The 11 U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows in each of the six trading sessions from May 15 through May 22, totalling $1.26B. Fidelity's FBTC led the redemptions for the week while BlackRock's IBIT also saw multi-session outflows; Morgan Stanley's MSBT pulled positive flows on a few days. The May 22 daily print was a $105M net outflow. Spot ether ETFs posted another $6.6M outflow on Friday — BlackRock's ETHA -$5.6M, Fidelity's FETH -$1M — extending their negative streak to 10 sessions.
explainer.howItWorks: The cumulative six-day drawdown is the worst weekly figure since late January 2026 and follows the May 16 selloff that took BTC to ~$77.6K on Hormuz-driven risk-off. The ether ETF 10-day outflow streak is the longest since March 2025. Drivers cited by The Block, Farside Investors and Santiment: surging long-end Treasury yields (30Y above 5.1%), a stronger dollar, U.S. April CPI at +3.8% Y/Y reigniting inflation concerns, and a deeper inflation-vs-rate-cut tension in the curve.
explainer.whyItMatters: ETF flows are the cleanest read on incremental U.S. institutional crypto demand. Six consecutive sessions of selling at this magnitude, paired with a 10-day ether ETF losing streak, signals that some allocators are rotating risk into the curve sell-off and away from beta. Counter-read from Santiment: ETF flows lean retail-driven, and sustained outflows have historically marked accumulation zones rather than starts of deeper declines. Key BTC level to watch: $74K, below which the contrarian buy signal would need to be reassessed.
explainer.forWho: crypto allocators, ETF-flow watchers, macro desks reading risk-off rotation

items.title: Trump says U.S.–Iran peace deal 'largely negotiated' on Saturday May 23 — Strait of Hormuz 'will be opened'; Iran's foreign ministry calls it a 30–60 day framework with nuclear off the table; BTC rebounds to ~$76.6K (+1.79%) on the news
items.summary: Trump posts on Truth Social Saturday that a U.S.–Iran agreement is 'largely negotiated' and the Strait of Hormuz 'will be opened.' Iran's foreign ministry calls it a 30–60 day framework with nuclear off the table; BTC +1.79% Saturday.

metrics.Hormuz tolls: Disputed — Iran's Fars says strait stays under Iranian management

explainer.tagline: Trump declares U.S.–Iran deal 'largely negotiated' with Strait of Hormuz reopening; Iran frames it as a 30–60 day framework, nuclear still off the table.
explainer.whatIsIt: On Saturday May 23, President Trump posted on Truth Social that an agreement with Iran has been 'largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries,' and that 'in addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened.' He said he held calls from the Oval Office with the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Bahrain, as well as Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu. The announcement caps a multi-week diplomatic push to end a war that has rattled global energy markets and pushed U.S. headline CPI to +3.8% Y/Y in April.
explainer.howItWorks: Trump's Truth Social post said 'final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly.' U.S. negotiators include VP JD Vance, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei characterized the document as a 30–60 day 'framework agreement' for future talks — not a final deal — emphasizing that nuclear issues are NOT part of current negotiations and that lifting sanctions remains a fixed Iranian position. Iran's Fars news agency separately disputed the Hormuz framing, saying the strait 'will still be under Iranian management' and that allowing ship traffic does not mean 'free passage,' contradicting the Trump line on tolls.
explainer.whyItMatters: Oil settled Friday at Brent $103.54 (-5%+ on the week) and WTI $96.60 (-8%+ on the week) on the de-escalation tape; a confirmed deal pressures Brent toward the $90s and unwinds the inflation pass-through that drove April PPI to +6.0% Y/Y. Bitcoin rebounded Saturday to ~$76,637 (+1.79%) after touching ~$74K earlier in the session — futures-style positioning ahead of Tuesday's U.S. open (markets closed Monday for Memorial Day). The framing gap between Trump and Tehran is what desks will price all weekend — especially on enriched uranium and Hormuz tolls, both of which Secretary Rubio flagged Thursday as deal-breakers if Iran pursues permanent control of shipping.
explainer.forWho: macro / energy / FX traders, oil & equity-index desks, crypto

explainer.tagline: Take-Two beats Q4 and prints first FY27 bookings guide with GTA VI dated Nov 19 — stock slips ~6% as Street wanted a bigger ramp.
explainer.whatIsIt: Take-Two reported Q4 FY26 (period ended March 31, 2026) on Thursday after the close, then traded down Friday despite a beat and a confirmed Grand Theft Auto VI launch date of November 19, 2026. The company laid out its first FY27 outlook, calling for $8.0–$8.2B of net bookings — roughly 20% growth on the FY26 record of $6.72B.
explainer.howItWorks: Q4 net bookings of $1.58B cleared the high end of the $1.51–$1.56B guide on GTA, Red Dead Redemption and mobile (Toon Blast +25%, Color Block Jam +15%). NBA 2K26 sold-in topped 10M units (+5% Y/Y); GTA V hit ~230M lifetime, with GTA Plus subscription contribution still growing. Recurrent consumer spending was 78% of bookings (+17% Y/Y). FY26 GAAP net loss was $59.5M, narrowing dramatically from a $3.73B loss in the year-ago period that was inflated by impairments. Operating cash flow finished the year at $624M vs the original $450M plan; FY27 OCF is now guided above $1B. The FY27 net bookings range of $8.0–$8.2B is shaped by the November 19 GTA VI launch.
explainer.whyItMatters: GTA VI is the single biggest catalyst on the consumer-software calendar — the date pins a ~4-month window into TTWO's FY27 and frames the bull/bear debate on initial launch sell-in, post-launch online monetisation, and the Switch 2 vs PS5/Xbox split. Friday's ~-6% reaction tells you the $8.0–$8.2B initial range — implying GTA VI plus the existing portfolio — was below the highest sell-side scenarios, but Zelnick called FY27 'a new record level of operating performance' and OCF >$1B is the cleaner read for compounders.

items.title: Qualcomm and Stellantis expand multi-year deal — Snapdragon Digital Chassis + Snapdragon Ride Pilot ADAS across STLA Brain next-gen vehicles globally, with non-binding LOI for Stellantis' aiMotive to join Qualcomm; QCOM +12% Friday
items.summary: Stellantis expands its Qualcomm deal to deploy Snapdragon Digital Chassis SoCs and Snapdragon Ride Pilot L2+ ADAS across STLA Brain vehicles; QCOM ~+12% Friday and signs a non-binding LOI to acquire Stellantis' aiMotive.

metrics.Scale: millions of vehicles across global Stellantis portfolio
metrics.ADAS scope: Snapdragon Ride Pilot for L2+ hands-free

explainer.tagline: Qualcomm wins the Stellantis car-software stack — Snapdragon Digital Chassis + Snapdragon Ride Pilot across STLA Brain, plus an LOI to acquire aiMotive.
explainer.whatIsIt: Stellantis and Qualcomm announced an expansion of their multi-year tech collaboration on Thursday, May 21, sending Qualcomm shares ~12% higher into Friday's close. Future Stellantis vehicles will be powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon Digital Chassis system-on-chips for cockpit, connectivity, and ADAS, integrated with Stellantis' STLA Brain software platform. The expansion adds Snapdragon Ride Pilot, an L2+ hands-free ADAS stack scalable from active safety to higher autonomy levels. Separately, the two signed a non-binding letter of intent for Stellantis' aiMotive automated-driving subsidiary to join Qualcomm.
explainer.howItWorks: Snapdragon Digital Chassis combines compute, connectivity and AI silicon in a unified family of SoCs. STLA Brain is Stellantis' EE/software architecture; the deal lets Stellantis standardise across its multi-brand portfolio (Jeep, Ram, Peugeot, Citroën, Fiat, Maserati, etc.) instead of bespoke per-brand stacks. Snapdragon Ride Pilot ships as a globally validated ADAS reference, taking Stellantis from active-safety packs to Level 2+ hands-free without rebuilding the pipeline per region. aiMotive — a Budapest-based simulation and automated-driving outfit Stellantis bought in 2022 — would fold into Qualcomm Automotive subject to diligence and regulatory approvals. No financial terms were disclosed for either the OEM award or the aiMotive LOI.
explainer.whyItMatters: Qualcomm's automotive run-rate is on a path past $5B in annual revenue, and locking in a top-5 global automaker on both the cockpit/ADAS SoCs and the L2+ stack defends that growth engine against NVIDIA DRIVE and Mobileye. Picking up aiMotive bolts a validated simulation/AD-software team onto Qualcomm Automotive. For Stellantis, the expanded standardisation is a cost-and-time-to-market story for the upcoming STLA-Brain wave. The +12% Friday move on QCOM reflects investors marking up the durability of Qualcomm Automotive's backlog and the optionality on higher-ASP ADAS attach.

items.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed Chair at the White House on May 22 — Justice Clarence Thomas administers oath in the East Room; first Fed Chair sworn in at the White House since Reagan/Greenspan in 1987; Trump says 'I want Kevin to be totally independent' before stumping for faster rate cuts
items.summary: Kevin Warsh is sworn in as the 11th modern-era Fed Chair in the White House East Room on May 22, with Justice Clarence Thomas administering the oath — a venue not used for the Fed Chair since Reagan/Greenspan in 1987.

metrics.Predecessor: Jerome Powell (stays as governor through Jan 2028)

explainer.tagline: Warsh takes the Fed gavel at a White House ceremony — symbolism that has Powell-era veterans watching independence cues.
explainer.whatIsIt: President Trump hosted Kevin Warsh's swearing-in as the 11th modern-era Federal Reserve Chair in the White House East Room on Friday, May 22. Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas administered the oath. Attendees included Justice Brett Kavanaugh, House Speaker Mike Johnson, NEC Director Kevin Hassett, Cabinet members and Warsh's wife Jane Lauder. The venue is itself the story: the last time a sitting Fed Chair was sworn in at the White House was Ronald Reagan's ceremony for Alan Greenspan in 1987.
explainer.howItWorks: Warsh, 56, was confirmed to the Fed Board 51–45 on May 12 and to the Chair on May 13, 54–45 — the narrowest Fed Chair confirmation margin on record. He succeeds Jerome Powell, who steps down as Chair after eight years but stays on as a governor through January 2028 (rare for an outgoing chair). Trump said at the ceremony, 'I want Kevin to be totally independent. Don't look at me, don't look at anybody' — but later at a campaign-style rally said interest rates would come down 'very quickly.' Warsh's own remarks emphasised pursuing 'price stability and maximum employment … with wisdom and clarity, independence and resolve.'
explainer.whyItMatters: The optics of an East Room ceremony followed hours later by the President publicly directing the rate path are exactly the tension the bond market is pricing. The April 28–29 FOMC minutes (released May 20) already showed an 8-4 hold with the most dissents since October 1992. Warsh inherits a curve where the 30Y has been making 19-year highs, headline CPI is +3.8% Y/Y, and the next FOMC is June 16-17. The first real signal will be Warsh's tone in his first FOMC press conference and whether the June dot plot starts pricing the Trump-favoured cut path.
explainer.forWho: macro traders, rates desks, Fed-independence watchers

items.title: SEC pauses Innovation Exemption framework for tokenized stocks on May 22 — pulls planned 'this week' release after Nasdaq, Cboe and CME flag investor-protection concerns; BTC slips ~3.6% below $76K and COIN -~4%
items.summary: SEC delays its tokenized-stocks Innovation Exemption framework after exchanges raised shareholder-rights and dividend-administration concerns; BTC drops ~3.6% below $76K and COIN ~-4% as the crypto-onto-Wall-Street narrative cools.

explainer.tagline: SEC blinks on tokenized stocks — exchanges flag shareholder-rights gaps and the agency holds the Innovation Exemption past its planned May release.
explainer.whatIsIt: Bloomberg reported on May 22 that the SEC has paused the rollout of its anticipated Innovation Exemption framework for tokenized stocks after meeting with stock-exchange officials and market participants who raised concerns. SEC staff had been on track to release the framework as soon as this week. The pause hit crypto on Friday: Bitcoin dropped ~3.6% intra-day, slipping under $76K, and Coinbase (COIN) traded ~4% lower, with the broader 'crypto-meets-equities' basket selling off in sympathy.
explainer.howItWorks: The Innovation Exemption would have created a regulatory sandbox letting crypto firms issue and trade blockchain-based 'tokenized' versions of regular U.S. equities, under a lighter touch than full broker-dealer/exchange registration. The most contentious piece was a provision that would have allowed third-party tokens — tokenized representations of company shares issued without the underlying company's involvement. That triggered exchange-side and corporate concerns about how dividends, voting, and shareholder rights would actually be administered if shares trade off-exchange on blockchain venues. SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce said publicly that the exemption was 'limited in scope and would facilitate trading only of digital representations of the same underlying equity security.' Chair Paul Atkins had signaled the framework would debut soon, but the agency has not formally withdrawn or revised the draft — the timeline is just slipping.
explainer.whyItMatters: The tokenized-stocks framework was the centerpiece of the Atkins-era SEC's promised 'crypto-onto-Wall-Street' agenda, and a near-term catalyst for COIN, Robinhood, Securitize/BlackRock BUIDL-style products, and the rest of the on-chain RWA complex. A pause — even without a formal kill — pushes out the timeline for spot tokenized equities and clouds Wall Street partnerships (Nasdaq, Cboe, CME) that had been preparing for adjacent infrastructure. BTC's Friday slide and COIN's ~4% drop are the cleanest read on how much of the 'TradFi rails' narrative was already in the tape.
explainer.forWho: crypto policy / regulatory desks, COIN longs, tokenized-RWA bulls

explainer.tagline: Estée Lauder walks away from the ~$40B Puig combination after Charlotte Tilbury change-of-control terms prove the sticking point.
explainer.whatIsIt: Estée Lauder said on Thursday May 21 / Friday May 22 2026 that both parties had terminated discussions of a combination first disclosed in March 2026. The collapse leaves the global prestige-beauty sector without its expected mega-deal anchor and removes a key M&A catalyst hanging over the sector. It also re-focuses the EL bull case on the standalone turnaround under de La Faverie, just as the broader beauty cohort (Coty, L'Oréal, Shiseido) faces tariff and China-recovery uncertainty.

items.title: Japan April 2026 CPI — core (ex fresh food) +1.4% Y/Y, lowest since March 2022 and well below +1.7% Reuters consensus; headline +1.4% (from +1.5%) and core-core +1.9% (from +2.4%) as energy falls 3.9% and cost-of-living offsets bite
items.summary: Japan April CPI undershoots: core (ex fresh food) +1.4% Y/Y vs +1.7% Reuters est, headline +1.4%, core-core +1.9%. Energy -3.9% and cost-of-living subsidies cool the print; markets still see BOJ moving to 1.00% in June.

explainer.tagline: Japan's core CPI slowed to a four-year low of 1.4% in April — but the BOJ is still tracking toward a June hike.
explainer.whatIsIt: Japan's Statistics Bureau released April 2026 nationwide CPI on May 22, 2026. Headline inflation eased to +1.4% Y/Y (from +1.5% in March) and core CPI (excluding fresh food) — the BOJ's most-watched gauge — slowed to +1.4% from +1.8%, undershooting all forecasts in a Reuters poll that had a +1.7% median.
explainer.howItWorks: Core-core CPI (ex food and energy), the gauge that tracks underlying services and goods, fell to +1.9% from +2.4% the prior month. Energy prices dropped 3.9% Y/Y, smaller than March's -5.7% decline but still a drag. Headline is now four straight months below the BOJ's 2% target, with government cost-of-living measures and softer processed-food prices cited as the main offsets to the lingering Iran-war energy shock.
explainer.whyItMatters: Despite the downside surprise, market consensus and Reuters reporting still place the June BOJ meeting as a likely venue for a 25bp hike to 1.00% from 0.75% — i.e., Ueda is treating the slowdown as transitory from energy subsidies. That keeps JPY traders watching tomorrow's MOF/BOJ communications closely. A softer-than-expected print would have meant clear yen weakness, but with the hike still in play, the cross stays in a tight range.
explainer.forWho: FX/macro traders, BOJ watchers

items.title: U.S. Commerce signs $2.013B CHIPS Act Letters of Intent with 9 quantum-computing firms — IBM $1B for new Albany 'Anderon' foundry, GlobalFoundries $375M, plus $100M each for Rigetti, D-Wave, Atom Computing, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum and Quantinuum (Diraq $38M); government takes minority non-controlling equity stakes
items.summary: Commerce Department signs 9 CHIPS Act letters of intent totaling $2.013B for U.S. quantum: IBM $1B, GlobalFoundries $375M, six $100M awards, plus Diraq $38M; RGTI +23%, QBTS +~20%, IBM +6.2%.

explainer.tagline: Washington's first big-money quantum bet: $2B in CHIPS Letters of Intent across 9 firms — and Uncle Sam takes minority equity in each.
explainer.whatIsIt: On May 21, 2026 the U.S. Department of Commerce announced it had signed Letters of Intent with nine American quantum-computing companies for $2.013B in CHIPS and Science Act incentives. The package is anchored by a proposed $1B IBM award to build 'Anderon', a new pure-play 300mm quantum wafer foundry in Albany, NY.
explainer.howItWorks: Awards: IBM $1B (matched by IBM with $1B cash for Anderon), GlobalFoundries $375M, $100M each to Atom Computing, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum, and Rigetti, and $38M to Diraq. As a condition of receiving funds, Commerce will take a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company. Anderon would serve multiple quantum hardware vendors with superconducting qubit wafers first.
explainer.whyItMatters: First federal-scale industrial policy for U.S. quantum, with the Commerce Department now also a quantum equity holder — mirroring the Intel CHIPS-equity precedent. RGTI ripped ~23%, QBTS ~20%, IBM +6.2%, IONQ +6.9% premarket despite not being on the award list. Quantum stocks turned a sub-sector that traded mostly on press-release tone into a CHIPS Act beneficiary.
explainer.forWho: policy desks, semis/AI infrastructure, quantum specialists
