items.title: Enbridge Q1 2026 — adj EBITDA $5.8B in line, secured backlog grows to $40B incl. 300 MW Cone Wind project for Meta
items.summary: Enbridge posts adj EPS $0.98 (vs $1.03 Y/Y), adj EBITDA $5.8B and DCF $3.9B; reaffirms FY26 guide. Sanctions ~$2B of new projects, including a 300 MW Cone Wind facility for Meta in Texas, lifting secured backlog to ~$40B.

explainer.tagline: Enbridge's Q1 lands in line, but the headline is a $40B secured backlog and a 300 MW Texas wind project tied to Meta data centers.
explainer.whatIsIt: Enbridge — North America's largest energy infrastructure company — reported Q1 2026 GAAP earnings of $1.7B ($0.77/sh) and adjusted earnings of $2.1B ($0.98/sh), with adjusted EBITDA of $5.8B essentially flat versus Q1 2025. Distributable cash flow rose to $3.9B from $3.8B and management reaffirmed FY26 guidance.
explainer.howItWorks: The bigger story is project sanctioning. ENB approved roughly $2B of new investments this quarter, including a US$0.7B / 300 MW Cone Wind facility in Texas supporting Meta data center load, a US$0.4B Tres Palacios gas storage expansion (25 Bcf), a Vector Pipeline expansion (400 MMcf/d westbound) and an 8 Bcf Dawn Hub storage expansion in Ontario. Combined, the secured capital backlog stepped up to ~$40B, with another ~$50B of unsanctioned opportunities in development.
explainer.whyItMatters: ENB is now openly booking renewables capacity into its backlog as AI-driven data center demand pulls hyperscalers into long-dated power deals — a structural shift for a name historically read as a midstream proxy. Reaffirming the $20.2–$20.8B EBITDA guide signals stability while the wind/storage sanctions push the post-2026 ~5% growth case.
explainer.forWho: midstream / energy infrastructure investors, AI-power thematic readers

items.title: Artivion Q1 2026 — revenue $116.3M (+18%), adj EBITDA +26% to $22.1M, but FY26 guide trimmed; exercises option to acquire Endospan for $175M
items.summary: Q1 revenue $116.3M (+18% reported, +12% cc), adj EBITDA $22.1M (+26%); but FY26 revenue guide trimmed to $480–$496M and EBITDA to $100–$107M on US AMDS and international weakness. AORT also exercises the Endospan option for $175M cash + up to $200M earn-outs.

explainer.tagline: Solid Q1 with stent grafts +21% and On-X +20%, but a softer FY guide and a $175M Endospan close knock AORT down hard.
explainer.whatIsIt: Artivion, the cardiac- and aortic-surgery medtech, reported Q1 2026 revenue of $116.3M (+18% GAAP, +12% constant currency) with adjusted EBITDA up 26% to $22.1M. Net income was $1.4M ($0.03/sh GAAP); non-GAAP EPS of $0.08 beat the Street's $0.06 print.
explainer.howItWorks: Product growth was led by stent grafts (+21%), On-X mechanical valves (+20%) and preservation services (+23%); BioGlue grew 4%. Despite the beat, management cut FY26 revenue guide to $480–$496M (from $486–$504M) and adjusted EBITDA to $100–$107M (from $105–$110M), citing US AMDS starter-set softness, weakness in Middle East stent-graft channels, supply chain bottlenecks and a 23% Latin America revenue decline. Separately, Artivion exercised its option to acquire Endospan now that the FDA PMA-approved NEXUS Aortic Arch System is in hand: base price $175M (net ~$135M after loan offsets), plus up to $200M of contingent consideration tied to future NEXUS performance, expected to close in Q2 2026.
explainer.whyItMatters: Two stories collide on one print — a clean operational quarter and a real guidance reset that the market punished hard, with shares dropping ~30% intraday. The Endospan exercise locks in NEXUS, the only PMA-approved aortic arch system, and signals AORT is willing to lever up the existing term loan to secure long-cycle stent-graft growth even as near-term execution slips.
explainer.forWho: medtech and small-cap healthcare investors

items.title: Western Midstream Q1 2026 — record $683M EBITDA (+15%), agrees to acquire Brazos Delaware II for ~$1.6B in cash + units
items.summary: Q1 EBITDA hits a record $683M (+15% Y/Y) on full Aris contribution and record Delaware Basin throughput; distribution +2.2% to $0.93/unit. WES also signs a $1.6B cash-and-unit deal for Brazos Delaware II.

explainer.tagline: Record midstream quarter doubles as a $1.6B Delaware Basin land grab — Brazos II adds ~470K acres and 460 MMcf/d.
explainer.whatIsIt: Western Midstream Partners — an Occidental-affiliated MLP — posted record Q1 2026 results and simultaneously announced its acquisition of privately held Brazos Delaware II for about $1.6B. Net income attributable to limited partners was $342.4M, Adj EBITDA $683.1M (+15% Y/Y), and Distributable Cash Flow $508.9M.
explainer.howItWorks: Q1 was driven by a full quarter of the Aris acquisition, record Delaware Basin crude/NGL throughput of 272 MBbls/d, and record produced-water throughput of 2,795 MBbls/d. The Brazos II deal is structured as $800M cash + $800M in WES common units; expected to close by end of Q2 2026 and contribute ~$100M of incremental Adj EBITDA in 2026. Quarterly distribution is raised 2.2% Q/Q to $0.930/unit, payable May 15.
explainer.whyItMatters: WES is doubling down on the Delaware Basin: ~470K dedicated acres and 460 MMcf/d of processing capacity bolted onto an already-record footprint. Management now expects 2026 results toward the high end of $2.50–$2.70B Adj EBITDA and $1.85–$2.05B DCF guides, contingent on commodity prices holding.
explainer.forWho: midstream/MLP and energy-yield investors

items.title: Corpay Q1 2026 — revenue $1.26B (+25%), adj EPS $5.80 (+29%), 11% organic growth; raises FY26 cash EPS guide to $26.30–$27.10; CPAY ~+11%
items.summary: Corpay Q1 revenue $1.26B (+25%) with 11% organic growth — fourth straight quarter at that pace — and adj EPS $5.80 (+29%). Lifts FY26 revenue guide to $5.25–$5.33B and cash EPS to $26.30–$27.10. Shares ~+11%.

explainer.tagline: Corporate-payments specialist beats and raises hard, sending CPAY ~11% higher.
explainer.whatIsIt: Corpay — the rebranded FleetCor — reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.26B, up 25% Y/Y, with organic revenue growth at 11% for the fourth straight quarter. Adjusted cash EPS was $5.80, up 29% from $4.51 a year ago, and GAAP EPS was $5.07.
explainer.howItWorks: Corporate Payments grew ~16% organically (~18% ex-float compression) and is now ~40% of revenue. Vehicle Payments grew ~10% while Lodging stabilized to flat. Management raised FY26 revenue guide to $5.25–$5.33B (from prior outlook), GAAP EPS to $20.39–$21.19, and adjusted cash EPS to $26.30–$27.10 (from prior $25.50–$26.50). Corpay also signed real-time blockchain-rails partnerships with JPMorgan and BVNK for B2B settlement.
explainer.whyItMatters: Corpay is the cleanest pure-play on B2B corporate payments — the guide raise materially exceeds the Q1 beat on its own, signaling sustained momentum into 2H. Read-across to other payments names (FIS, FI, GPN). Float-compression dynamics mean the org-growth pace looks even better when stripped out.
explainer.forWho: fintech / payments investors

items.title: Aeva Q1 2026 — record $6.3M revenue (+86%), ships production-intent Atlas LiDAR to Daimler Truck; named NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion reference outside China
items.summary: Aeva posts record Q1 revenue of $6.3M (+86% Y/Y), GAAP loss $35M ($0.56/sh). Shipped production-intent Atlas long-range LiDAR to Daimler Truck and was selected as the reference LiDAR for NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion outside China.

explainer.tagline: Record quarter pairs with two trophy partnerships — Daimler trucks and NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion.
explainer.whatIsIt: Aeva, the FMCW LiDAR maker, posted Q1 2026 revenue of $6.3M (vs $3.4M a year ago, +86%). GAAP operating loss was $35.1M and GAAP net loss was $35.0M, or $0.56/share. Two go-to-market milestones bracket the quarter.
explainer.howItWorks: Aeva delivered production-intent Atlas sensors to Daimler Truck — a step toward series production as the exclusive long-range LiDAR supplier on Daimler's autonomous-truck program. First Atlas Ultra units shipped into a global top-10 European passenger OEM Level-3 program with a 2028 SOP target. NVIDIA selected Aeva as the reference LiDAR supplier for DRIVE Hyperion outside China. Available liquidity stood at $224.5M.
explainer.whyItMatters: Aeva is small but the customer logos are real: serial Daimler truck integration is the first FMCW production-intent LiDAR program of its kind, and the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion reference position routes Aeva into every Hyperion-based OEM's L3+ stack outside China. Read-across to LIDR, INVZ, OUST, MVIS.

items.title: Toyota FY26 — record ¥50.7T revenue but op income -21.5% on ¥1.38T US tariff hit; FY27 guide cuts another 20% to ¥3T
items.summary: Toyota's fiscal 2026 (Apr 2025–Mar 2026) printed record net revenue of ¥50.7T and 9.6M global units, but op income fell 21.5% to ¥3.77T as US tariffs cost ¥1.38T and dragged North America to a ¥298.6B loss.

explainer.tagline: Record sales year, but the US tariff bill turned Toyota's North American operation into a $2B loss.
explainer.whatIsIt: Toyota Motor Corporation reported full-year FY2026 results on May 8 (covering April 2025–March 2026). Vehicle sales hit a record 9.595M units, revenue rose 5.5% to ¥50.68T, but operating income fell 21.5% to ¥3.77T and Q4 op income missed badly at ¥569.4B vs ¥813.3B Street estimate.
explainer.howItWorks: Toyota disclosed a ¥1.38T (~$9B) operating-income hit from US tariffs in FY26, plus a ¥2.03T currency drag. North America (excluding interest-rate-swap valuation effects) swung from a ¥108.8B profit to a ¥298.6B (~$2.0B) operating loss even though regional volumes grew 8.5%. Europe and Asia held positive, but Q4 group volume slipped to 2.29M units. For FY27 (ending March 2027), Toyota guides operating income to ¥3.0T — another roughly 20% reduction — including an additional ¥670B tariff hit on a 150 yen/USD assumption.
explainer.whyItMatters: Toyota is the world's largest automaker by units, and this is the cleanest read yet on how Section 232/IEEPA-era US auto tariffs flow through a Japanese OEM's P&L. Tokyo shares closed -2.18% at ¥2,913. The tariff regime here is the same one the US Court of International Trade ruled unlawful for the 10% Section 122 duties this week — but auto tariffs were on a separate authority and are not affected by that ruling, so the FY27 guide builds them in. Read-through to other Japanese/Korean OEMs (Honda, Nissan, Hyundai) and US-listed parts suppliers (BWA, MGA, ALV).
explainer.forWho: auto desks, macro/tariff watchers, Japan/EM equity

items.title: AWS US-East-1 thermal event takes Coinbase offline ~7 hours, hits FanDuel and CME — single-AZ outage cascades
items.summary: AWS Northern Virginia data center overheated late May 7, knocking out the use1-az4 availability zone. Coinbase trading was down ~7 hours; FanDuel and CME Group also hit. Several services still impaired into May 8.

explainer.tagline: An overheated data hall in northern Virginia took down a slice of the cloud — and the consumer apps that quietly run on it.
explainer.whatIsIt: On May 7 around 4:20 PM PDT, AWS reported a thermal event in a single availability zone (use1-az4) of its US-East-1 region in Northern Virginia. EC2 instances and EBS volumes lost power, and a slate of higher-level services degraded as failover did not behave as designed. Recovery extended into May 8 as cooling capacity was rebuilt incrementally.
explainer.howItWorks: Power to the affected hardware was restored by 9:12 PM PDT, but services like ElastiCache, MSK (Kafka) and OpenSearch remained impaired hours later. Coinbase users were locked out of trades, balance checks and withdrawals for roughly seven hours; the exchange noted custody systems were unaffected. FanDuel users could not cash out mid-game; CME Group's trading platform was also disrupted.
explainer.whyItMatters: It is the second material AWS-driven Coinbase outage since October 2025 and lands the same day Coinbase reported a $394M Q1 GAAP loss. The pattern keeps reopening the question of single-region concentration risk for crypto exchanges, sportsbooks and U.S. derivatives venues that all sit on the same Virginia footprint.
explainer.forWho: infra teams, crypto traders, sportsbook bettors, exchange-risk desks

items.title: Vital Farms Q1 2026 — revenue +15.4% to $187.2M but loss of $0.03/sh, FY26 EBITDA guide cut to $0–$10M and butter business wound down; VITL ~-24%
items.summary: Vital Farms beat on revenue ($187.2M, +15.4%) but flipped to a $1.5M net loss as gross margin collapsed from 38.5% to 28.3% on egg oversupply. FY26 EBITDA guide slashed to $0–$10M and the butter business is being wound down; VITL fell ~24% to $9.11.

explainer.tagline: An egg oversupply blew up Vital Farms' margin, dragged Q1 to a loss and forced a deep guide cut plus a butter exit.
explainer.whatIsIt: Vital Farms reported Q1 2026 results after the close on May 7. Revenue grew 15.4% Y/Y to $187.2M, but GAAP swung to a $1.5M net loss versus a $16.9M profit a year earlier. The company also said it will wind down its butter product line by year-end to refocus on the core egg business.
explainer.howItWorks: Gross margin compressed from 38.5% to 28.3% as egg oversupply pushed sales into lower-priced wholesale and breaker channels. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $5.0M from $27.5M. Management cut FY26 revenue guide to $775–$800M (still ≥5% growth), adjusted EBITDA guide to $0–$10M (which embeds about $32M of oversupply-management costs), and capex to $70–$75M from a prior $140–$150M plan.
explainer.whyItMatters: The print recasts VITL from a high-multiple consumer-staples grower into a margin-restoration story. The butter exit and capex cut signal management is conserving cash through an industry oversupply cycle. Shares dropped roughly 24% to $9.11, near a 52-week low.
explainer.forWho: consumer-staples PMs, small-cap growth funds, ag-economy watchers

items.title: U.S. Court of International Trade rules Trump's 10% global Section 122 tariffs unlawful in 2-1 panel decision
items.summary: A three-judge CIT panel ruled 2-1 that Trump exceeded his authority under Section 122 of the Trade Act when he imposed the February 2026 10% global tariff. Permanent injunction applies only to the named plaintiffs.

explainer.tagline: CIT strikes down Trump's second-attempt 10% global tariffs as unlawful under Section 122 — but only the three plaintiffs get relief.
explainer.whatIsIt: The U.S. Court of International Trade ruled 2-1 in Burlap and Barrel, Inc. v. Trump that the 10% global import surcharge Trump imposed in February 2026 — after the Supreme Court struck down his earlier IEEPA-based 'Liberation Day' tariffs — was unlawful. The court held the administration could not invoke Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 because that statute requires a balance-of-payments deficit, not a goods trade deficit.
explainer.howItWorks: A three-judge CIT panel issued a 53-page opinion finding the administration conflated balance-of-payments deficits with trade deficits to justify the tariffs. The permanent injunction was narrow: tariffs cannot be charged on imports of the three plaintiffs (Burlap and Barrel, Basic Fun, the State of Washington) and refunds with interest are owed on duties already paid by them. Claims by 23 other states were dismissed for lack of standing. The administration is expected to appeal to the Federal Circuit and ultimately the Supreme Court.
explainer.whyItMatters: Two of Trump's two tariff legal vehicles have now been struck down — IEEPA at the Supreme Court in February and Section 122 at the CIT now. With CBP CAPE refunds already starting on the IEEPA tariffs, importers and corporates are running scenarios for either a third legal theory or a Federal Circuit reversal. The narrow injunction means most importers still pay the 10% for now, but the precedent makes a broader injunction or class-wide refund more likely if the appeal fails.
explainer.forWho: macro traders, importers, retailers, supply-chain analysts

items.title: U.S. April 2026 jobs report — payrolls +115K beat 62K est, unemployment steady at 4.3%, March revised up to +185K

explainer.tagline: April payrolls almost double consensus and March revised higher — labor market still resilient as Fed weighs cuts.
explainer.whatIsIt: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the April 2026 Employment Situation report on Friday, May 8 at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the first jobs print since the FOMC's late-April hold, and the input most watched into the June 16–17 meeting.
explainer.howItWorks: Total nonfarm payrolls rose 115,000 in April vs the 62,000 LSEG / 65,000 FactSet consensus. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3%. February was revised down 23K to -156K and March revised up 7K to +185K, leaving the two-month net 16K lower. Health care, transportation and warehousing, and retail trade were the largest contributors; federal government payrolls continued to fall. Average workweek ticked up 0.1 hr to 34.3.
explainer.whyItMatters: Back-to-back monthly gains for the first time in roughly a year argue against the recession framing some had built around February's negative print. With unemployment steady, the cooling-but-resilient narrative holds: rates desks priced odds of a June cut lower, and longer-end Treasury yields had spent the week hovering around the 5% line on the 30-year. Growth-sensitive equities and small caps benefit if prints keep landing in the 'soft landing' window.

items.title: First wave of $166B Trump tariff refunds begins paying out via CBP CAPE system; refunds scheduled to ramp from May 12
items.summary: Trade lawyers told Bloomberg some clients have received tariff refund payments as of May 6, with the first batch of broad refunds scheduled to start May 12. CBP is consolidating ~$166B in IEEPA duties paid by 333,000+ importers via a new CAPE portal.

explainer.tagline: Importers start cashing in on the Supreme Court's IEEPA tariff ruling.
explainer.whatIsIt: U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) tool, launched April 20, is now actively paying refunds to importers who paid tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) before the Supreme Court invalidated those tariffs in February 2026. Bloomberg reported on May 6 that the first refund payments have hit importers' bank accounts.
explainer.howItWorks: More than 333,000 importers paid roughly $166B across ~53M shipments while the IEEPA tariffs were in effect. CAPE consolidates refund claims rather than processing entry-by-entry; CBP estimates 60–90 days from claim acceptance to payout. The first wave of broad refunds is scheduled to begin May 12. The Supreme Court ruled in February that the use of IEEPA to impose global tariffs exceeded presidential authority, with Congress holding the constitutional power to impose tariffs.
explainer.whyItMatters: $166B is a meaningful liquidity injection back into U.S. importers — retailers, electronics distributors, auto-parts firms — and removes a tail risk that has been weighing on covered names. It also underscores that any future tariff strategy needs a different statutory basis (Section 122 has been used for a 10% global rate through July 24). Watch retailer margins, freight forwarders, and small-cap consumer names that disclosed material tariff exposure for upgrades on confirmed cash receipts.
explainer.forWho: Macro traders, retail / freight / consumer discretionary specialists

explainer.howItWorks: Revenue came in at $2.709B, up 35.1% Y/Y and ahead of the $2.62B Street consensus, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.87 versus $0.81 expected. Non-GAAP gross margin was 62.4%, inside Arista's 62%–63% guide but down from 63.4% the prior quarter on customer mix and rising supply-chain costs. After an 87% YTD-prior rally, investors took profits on a stock trading near 39× forward earnings, dragging AI-networking peers and read-throughs to NVDA's networking partners.

items.title: Brent crashes below $100 (-8.2%), WTI -9.8% as Trump pauses Project Freedom; US-Iran near 14-point peace MOU
items.summary: Brent fell 8.2% to $100.83 and WTI fell 9.8% to $92.28 after Trump paused the Project Freedom escort and the White House signaled a 14-point memorandum to end the Iran war is near.

explainer.tagline: Brent collapses below $100 as Trump halts Project Freedom escort and Washington and Tehran inch toward a 14-point peace memo.
explainer.whatIsIt: Crude oil sold off sharply on May 6 after Axios reported the White House was nearing a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding with Iran to end the two-month war. Trump paused 'Project Freedom,' the US Navy effort that had begun a day earlier to escort merchant vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, citing diplomatic progress.
explainer.howItWorks: Brent for July delivery slipped 8.2% to $100.83 in early US trading, with prices briefly trading below $100 intraday. WTI fell 9.8% to $92.28. Iran's foreign ministry said it was 'evaluating' Washington's 14-point proposal, which reportedly covers a uranium enrichment moratorium, sanctions relief, frozen-fund distribution, and Hormuz access. Only two merchant ships had transited the escorted route before Trump halted it.
explainer.whyItMatters: Energy desks had positioned for prolonged Hormuz disruption with Brent peaking near $126 last week; today's move unwinds a chunk of that risk premium in hours. If the memo holds, headline CPI pressure eases and Treasury yields ease at the long end (the US 30Y just topped 5% on oil-driven inflation fears). A breakdown in talks reverses all of it, and Trump warned bombing would resume 'at a much higher level' if Iran walks.
explainer.forWho: energy desks, macro traders

items.title: Strategy Q1 2026 — $12.54B net loss on BTC mark-down, holdings reach 818,334 BTC; Saylor opens door to selective bitcoin sales
items.summary: Strategy reported a $12.54B Q1 net loss on $14.46B unrealized BTC losses; holdings reached 818,334 BTC at ~$75,537 avg cost; Saylor said on the call the firm 'will probably sell some bitcoin to pay a dividend'.

explainer.tagline: Strategy books a $12.54B Q1 loss on bitcoin mark-down and Saylor floats selling BTC to fund dividends — a break from the 'never sell' line.
explainer.whatIsIt: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) reported Q1 2026 results after the close on May 5. The company logged a $12.54B net loss (-$38.25/diluted share), driven by $14.46B in unrealized bitcoin valuation losses as BTC sold off in Q1. Holdings reached 818,334 BTC, around 3.9% of the eventual 21M supply.
explainer.howItWorks: Average cost basis is $75,537/BTC against a market price near $78,374 at quarter-end, leaving the position barely above water. Operating revenue grew 11.9% Y/Y to $124.3M. Strategy raised $7.37B through ATM offerings in Q1 and another $4.32B between April 1 and May 3, taking 2026 capital raised to $11.68B. The company runs roughly $1.5B in annual dividend obligations across its preferred stack (STRC alone scaled to $8.5B). On the call, executive chair Michael Saylor said the firm 'will probably sell some bitcoin to pay a dividend just to inoculate the market and send the message that we did it' — a notable shift from the long-running 'never sell' line.
explainer.whyItMatters: Strategy is the largest corporate bitcoin holder and a benchmark for the BTC-treasury cohort. Any signal it might trim shifts how the market reads forced-seller risk in a drawdown, and explains why MSTR fell ~4% after-hours and BTC slipped below $81K. Other BTC-treasury names (METAPLANET, MARA, RIOT) read across.

items.title: Novo Nordisk Q1 2026 — Wegovy pill drives 'strongest-ever' GLP-1 launch, raises FY26 guide; NVO +6.7% in Copenhagen
items.summary: Adjusted operating profit DKK 32.9B, Wegovy pill prescriptions topped 2M since the January US launch, and Novo narrowed FY26 adjusted sales/profit guidance to -4 to -12% from -5 to -13% prior. Shares jumped in Copenhagen.

explainer.tagline: Wegovy pill launch beats expectations, prompting Novo to lift the floor of its FY26 guide despite Lilly's competing Foundayo.
explainer.whatIsIt: Novo Nordisk reported Q1 2026 results that beat operating profit expectations, driven by its newly-launched Wegovy oral GLP-1 pill which has hit ~2M prescriptions since the January 5 US launch. The company narrowed its 2026 outlook to a -4 to -12% adjusted sales contraction (vs. -5 to -13% prior) and a matching range on adjusted operating profit growth.
explainer.howItWorks: Reported Q1 net sales of DKK 96.8B were +32% at constant currency, lifted by a one-time 340B Medicaid rebate provision reversal. On an adjusted basis (excluding that reversal), sales were DKK 70.1B (-4% CER) and adjusted operating profit DKK 32.9B (-6% CER). Wegovy injection sales of DKK 18.2B grew 12% Y/Y. The Wegovy pill, launched in the US on January 5, has accumulated more than 2M prescriptions including ~1.3M in Q1 alone, with weekly Rx volumes exceeding 200K by the week of April 17 — what Novo calls the strongest-ever GLP-1 launch by US volume.
explainer.whyItMatters: The pill ramp eases concerns that Eli Lilly's Foundayo (orforglipron, FDA-approved early April) would steal the oral GLP-1 category outright; Lilly disclosed >20K patient starts on Foundayo in early weeks while Novo's Wegovy commands ~65% of new US Rx. NVO trades far below its 2024 highs after a brutal 12-month derate; today's guide bump is the first upside revision since the Wegovy pill approval cycle. Watch Eli Lilly's response on Q2 calls.

explainer.howItWorks: The company built 5,500 vehicles, up 149% year over year, but only delivered 3,093 — a flat number versus Q1 2025 — after a seat-supplier issue knocked Lucid Gravity production offline for 29 days in February. GAAP gross margin deteriorated to -110% on lower volumes and reduced regulatory-credit sales. Lucid finished the quarter with $0.7B of cash and $3.2B of total liquidity, pro forma $4.7B after April's $1.05B capital raise (PIF $550M convertible preferred, $300M common offering, $200M from Uber).
explainer.whyItMatters: The miss undercuts the bull case that Gravity ramps would deliver an inflection in 2026, and inventory is now elevated heading into Q2, with management saying it will adjust production to demand. The Uber robotaxi expansion to a 35,000-vehicle minimum and Saudi PIF support keep the runway intact, but the gap between production and deliveries plus a -110% gross margin keep the cash-burn question front and center.

items.summary: U.S. Navy launches Operation Project Freedom to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM says the U.S.-Iran ceasefire holds despite UAE strikes; Brent settles ~$109.87 (-4%), WTI ~$102.27.

explainer.tagline: Day one of the U.S. Navy's Hormuz escort mission, with oil giving back most of the prior session's spike.
explainer.whatIsIt: After Iranian drone and missile strikes on the UAE on Monday sent Brent up nearly 6% to $114, the U.S. on Tuesday operationalised 'Project Freedom' — a CENTCOM-led mission to escort merchant ships through the Strait of Hormuz, with the USS Tripoli amphibious group plus destroyers and 15,000 personnel.
explainer.howItWorks: Brent settled at roughly $109.87 (-4%) and WTI at $102.27 (-3.9%) as CENTCOM and the State Department said the U.S.-Iran ceasefire is intact despite the UAE attacks. The U.S. has destroyed 7 Iranian fast boats so far; ~1,500 vessels carrying ~22,500 crew remain stranded in the Gulf, and only a handful of merchant ships have actually transited under escort.
explainer.whyItMatters: Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of seaborne crude. The day's pullback is conditional on the ceasefire holding — any new strike on tankers or U.S. ships would re-price Brent quickly. Energy names (XLE, OXY, XOM), refiners, airlines, and the long end of the Treasury curve are the most direct read-throughs.

items.title: eBay rejects GameStop's ~$56B unsolicited bid as 'neither credible nor attractive'; Cohen weighs hostile move
items.summary: eBay's board on May 12 formally rejected GameStop's $125/share offer, citing financing uncertainty around TD Securities' $20B letter, governance concerns and 'operational risks'. Chair Paul Pressler called it 'neither credible nor attractive'; CEO Ryan Cohen may take the bid hostile.

metrics.Debt financing: Up to $20B highly-confident letter from TD Securities
metrics.Possible next step: Hostile tender / proxy at eBay shareholders

explainer.tagline: eBay's board calls GameStop's $125/share bid not credible and unattractive, leaving Ryan Cohen with a hostile path or a walk-away.
explainer.whatIsIt: On May 12, eBay's board formally rejected GameStop's unsolicited $125/share, 50% cash / 50% stock proposal first announced May 3. Chair Paul Pressler said the offer was 'neither credible nor attractive', citing six factors including financing uncertainty, governance and operational risks, and a leadership structure the board found unworkable. CEO Ryan Cohen had previewed willingness to take the bid hostile if the board demurred.
explainer.howItWorks: GameStop's offer represented a 46% premium to eBay's unaffected Feb 4 close and a 36% premium to its 90-day VWAP, structured as roughly $9.4B of GameStop balance-sheet cash plus a highly-confident $20B debt letter from TD Securities. eBay's board flagged the cash leg as effectively unfunded given the size, and questioned whether a combined entity could absorb the leverage. A hostile tender or proxy at eBay's shareholders is the next available lever for Cohen.
explainer.whyItMatters: The rejection caps the formal courtship phase and shifts the next move to GameStop. EBAY rose ~5% on the original news May 4 and GameStop fell about 10%; M&A arb spreads are now functions of whether Cohen finances a sweetened bid or attempts a shareholder end-run. Without a stronger financing package, the deal probability tightens.
explainer.forWho: M&A arb desks, e-commerce and collectibles investors

items.title: Amazon opens its full logistics network to outside businesses, sending UPS ~10% lower and FedEx ~9% lower
items.summary: Amazon launched Amazon Supply Chain Services, exposing its freight, fulfillment and parcel network to any business; UPS fell about 10% and FedEx fell roughly 9% on the day.

metrics.Anchor customers disclosed: Procter & Gamble, 3M, Lands' End, American Eagle Outfitters
metrics.Channels supported: Amazon, Walmart, Shopify, TikTok and others

explainer.tagline: Amazon turns its logistics stack into a third-party offering, branded Amazon Supply Chain Services.
explainer.whatIsIt: Amazon launched Amazon Supply Chain Services on May 4, packaging its freight (ocean, air, ground, rail), distribution, fulfillment and parcel-shipping operations into a single offering open to any business — including sellers on Walmart, Shopify, TikTok and other competing marketplaces. The launch was framed by Amazon as a logistics analogue to AWS, and Procter & Gamble, 3M, Lands' End and American Eagle Outfitters were named as initial customers.
explainer.howItWorks: Customers sign up through a single portal at supplychain.amazon.com and can mix-and-match freight, distribution, fulfillment and parcel services. Amazon says the network is the same one used internally for its own retail operations and existing third-party seller fulfillment, with optimization driven by its AI demand-forecasting models. Peter Larsen, VP of Amazon Supply Chain Services, drew an explicit comparison to AWS in the launch materials.
explainer.whyItMatters: UPS fell roughly 10% and FedEx fell about 9% on the launch day, with sell-side notes flagging it as a direct competitive blow to traditional parcel carriers. Contract logistics and 3PL operators including DHL Supply Chain, GXO and Maersk Logistics are also exposed if Amazon scales the offering aggressively. The next read-throughs are pricing and contract terms versus incumbent quotes — UPS and FedEx Q1 commentary becomes the sector's pressure point.
explainer.forWho: logistics, transports and large-cap e-commerce investors

FY 2026 guidance now calls for transaction-margin dollars to show a slight decline and adjusted EPS to range from a low-single-digit decline to slightly positive vs FY25's $5.31. The company kept a $6B buyback authorization and at least $6B of adjusted FCF for the year.
explainer.whyItMatters: The print is the cleanest signal yet that PayPal's branded-checkout reacceleration is being paid for with margin. A slight FY transaction-margin-dollar decline coming into the year was not in the buy-side base case, and the ~10% drop reprices a name that had been working as a low-multiple turnaround.
explainer.forWho: fintech analysts, value/turnaround funds

items.title: Iran drone strike sets fire at UAE Fujairah oil hub; Brent jumps 5.8% to $114
items.summary: An Iranian drone strike ignited a fire at the UAE's Fujairah Oil Industry Zone on May 4, breaking the April 8 ceasefire. UAE intercepted three of four Iranian missiles. Brent crude settled +5.8% at $114.44; WTI +4.39% at $106.42.

explainer.tagline: First Iranian strike on UAE soil since the April 8 ceasefire reignites the Gulf war premium and sends Brent to four-year highs.
explainer.whatIsIt: On May 4 the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone caught fire after an Iranian drone strike, while UAE air defenses intercepted three of four incoming Iranian cruise missiles, with a fourth crashing at sea. Three Indian nationals were injured. It was the first attack on the UAE since the April 8 U.S.–Iran ceasefire.
explainer.howItWorks: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps published a map expanding its claimed control zone to cover Fujairah and Khorfakkan ports and the Umm Al Quwain coast. Fujairah sits at the end of the Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, making it critical to UAE exports during the conflict. Brent settled +5.8% at $114.44 and WTI +4.39% at $106.42.
explainer.whyItMatters: The break in the ceasefire reopens the path to a sustained oil-supply premium and feeds inflation expectations: rate-cut odds for the next FOMC moved further out, and 30Y Treasury yields breached 5% the same day on the inflation read-through. Energy desks now have to price the option that Fujairah-style strikes recur and Hormuz transit risk gets repriced higher.
explainer.forWho: energy desks, macro traders

items.title: 30-year Treasury yield breaches 5% for first time since July 2025 as oil-driven inflation bites
items.summary: The 30Y UST yield touched 5.03% on May 4, breaching 5% for the first time since July 2025, as the Fujairah strike and rising oil pushed inflation expectations higher. 10Y rose to 4.456%; mortgage rates climbed to 6.52%.

explainer.tagline: Long-end Treasuries crack 5% as the Iran-driven oil spike pulls inflation expectations higher.
explainer.whatIsIt: On May 4 the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield gained more than 5 basis points to 5.021%, with an intraday high of 5.03% — the first close above 5% since July 2025. The 10-year rose to 4.456%, the highest since July 2025.
explainer.howItWorks: The move came alongside Brent +5.8% to $114 after the Iranian drone strike on Fujairah. Long-end yields lead because the inflation pass-through from oil compounds across the curve. Per market pricing on the day, Fed-rate-hike odds moved up to roughly 80% for the next meeting, and Barclays and Morgan Stanley pushed back their rate-cut expectations.
explainer.whyItMatters: 5% on the long bond is a psychological line that ties refi-sensitive sectors (housing, REITs, regional banks) to a fresh leg of duration risk. The 30Y mortgage rate climbing to 6.52% extends the housing-affordability squeeze. For risk assets, the move is the second-order effect of the Gulf escalation — even if oil pulls back, the inflation-expectations channel has been re-anchored higher.
explainer.forWho: rates desks, mortgage REIT and bank holders

items.title: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs draw $532M on May 4 — third straight day of net inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in $532.19M on May 4, a third consecutive day of inflows. BlackRock IBIT led with $335M, Fidelity FBTC added $185M, Morgan Stanley MSBT pulled $12M.

explainer.tagline: Spot BTC ETFs took in another $532M on May 4, with BlackRock and Fidelity capturing nearly all of it.
explainer.whatIsIt: U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows of $532.19M on Monday, May 4 — the third consecutive day of net additions. BlackRock's IBIT pulled $335.46M, Fidelity's FBTC took $184.57M, and Morgan Stanley's MSBT added $12.16M.
explainer.howItWorks: The cluster of inflows comes against an Iran-driven risk-off backdrop and follows a $629M day on Friday May 1. April logged $2.44B in net inflows — the strongest monthly figure since October 2025. Cumulative net inflows since the January 2024 launch sit at roughly $58.7B, still shy of the October peak around $61.2B.
explainer.whyItMatters: BTC ETF flows are the cleanest read on incremental institutional bid. Three straight days of net inflows during a Gulf-driven oil and rates spike suggests bitcoin is being treated as a duration-light hedge by some of the same allocators selling long Treasuries. Watch the IBIT/FBTC concentration — flows remain dominated by two issuers.
explainer.forWho: crypto allocators, ETF-flow watchers
